title: Crash on launch on Windows when the Intel OpenGL driver is present (igvk64.dll access violation)
author: zaum
body:
## Summary

`printcraft.exe` crashes immediately on launch on Windows 11 — both the installed (MSI) build and the portable build. No window appears; the process exits with `0xC0000005` (access violation).

`printcraft-cli` works fine, so this affects the GUI only. The crash happens during window / render-backend initialisation.

## Environment

| | |
|---|---|
| OS | Windows 11 (10.0.26100) |
| PrintCraft | 0.2.0 (`printcraft.exe`, version stamp `0x6ac34a3a`) |
| GPU | Intel UHD Graphics 630 + NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5060 Ti |
| Intel driver | `31.0.101.2145` (DCH) |
| NVIDIA driver | `32.0.16.1714` |

## Crash signature

```
Faulting application name: printcraft.exe, version: 0.2.0.0
Faulting module name: igvk64.dll, version: 31.0.101.2145
Exception code: 0xc0000005
Faulting application path: C:\Program Files\PrintCraft\printcraft.exe
Faulting module path: C:\Windows\System32\DriverStore\FileRepository\iigd_dch.inf_amd64_98d08511a5a11871\igvk64.dll
```

The crash always lands inside `igvk64.dll` (the Intel OpenGL driver). A dump of the crashed process shows the `wgpu` graphics stack loading `opengl32.dll` / `glu32.dll` and the Intel OpenGL ICDs (`igvk64.dll`, `ig9icd64.dll`, `igdml64.dll`) into the **main** process before it dies — so the Intel OpenGL driver is exercised in-process rather than in a separate GPU worker.

## Reproduction

1. Install `printcraft-0.2.0-windows-x64.msi` (or unpack the portable build).
2. Launch PrintCraft.
3. The process exits after a couple of seconds with exit code `-1073741819` (`0xC0000005`). No window appears.

## What did not help

Chromium/Electron-style GPU switches have no effect, which is consistent with the crash happening in the main process (this app is Rust + egui/wgpu rather than Electron):

- `--disable-gpu`
- `--disable-gpu --disable-gpu-compositing`
- `--disable-gpu --disable-software-rasterizer`
- `--use-angle=swiftshader`
- `--use-gl=swiftshader`
- `--in-process-gpu`
- `--disable-features=DirectComposition`
- `WGPU_ADAPTE…

title: Windows v0.2.0: launching PrintCraft opens a console window, and the Start Menu shortcut has no icon
author: MikailuReeves
body:
Console window: `printcraft.exe` is built with the console subsystem (PE subsystem 3), so Windows opens a terminal next to the app. `apps/printcraft/src/main.rs` needs, at the top:
```
#![cfg_attr(all(windows, not(debug_assertions)), windows_subsystem = "windows")]
```

Blank icon: in `packaging/windows/printcraft.wxs`, the Icon Id `PrintcraftIcon` has no extension. Windows Installer requires Icon names to end in `.ico`/`.exe` for advertised shortcuts and ARPPRODUCTICON. Rename to `PrintcraftIcon.ico` (lines 27, 28, 49).

The icon embedded in the exe via build.rs is fine only the MSI reference is broken.

title: [Bug] Dynamically update of signature visual appearance on canvas upon successful validation ("green tick" one) not working
author: sp8996
body: Currently, PrintCraft successfully performs cryptographic validation of digital signatures (showing "Signed and all signatures are valid" in the top banner and signature panel). However, it does not dynamically update the visual appearance of the signature widget on the document canvas itself. Many government-issued PDFs (such as Indian e-District certificates) are generated with a static image of a yellow question mark and the text "Signature Not Verified" baked into the PDF's default Appearance Stream (/AP dictionary). When Adobe Acrobat successfully validates these signatures, it dynamically hides this default appearance and overlays a green checkmark. PrintCraft currently leaves the original yellow question mark on the canvas, which causes confusion for users printing the document, even though the signature panel confirms it is valid. Steps to Reproduce: 1. Open a PDF containing a digital signature that has a default "unverified" visual appearance (e.g., a yellow question mark). 2. Ensure the signer's certificate is trusted so that PrintCraft successfully validates it. 3. Look at the top banner and the right-hand Signature Panel (it will correctly say "Signature is valid"). 4. Look at the signature on the actual document canvas. Expected Behavior: Once the signature is cryptographically validated, PrintCraft should dynamically update the visual appearance of the signature widget on the canvas to reflect the valid state (e.g., overlaying a green checkmark or hiding the "Not Verified" text), achieving parity with Adobe Acrobat. Actual Behavior: The signature panel correctly shows the signature as valid, but the document canvas continues to display the static, baked-in "Signature Not Verified" / yellow "?" image. Screenshots are attached as well as the screenshot of expected behavior as observed in Acrobat. Environment: OS: CachyOS PrintCraft Version: 0.2.1 (Appimage)

title: PDF JavaScript launchURL opens external URLs without confirmation or scheme validation
author: Harshith292002
body:
## Summary

`app.launchURL()` from Acrobat-compatible PDF JavaScript opens an arbitrary URL in the system browser with no confirmation dialog and no URL-scheme allowlist. Combined with JavaScript being **enabled by default**, a malicious PDF can exfiltrate form field values (or other script-readable data) by constructing a URL and calling `launchURL`.

This weakens the documented claim that scripts run in a sandbox without network access (Preferences ▸ JavaScript UI copy).

## Environment

- Repo tag: `v0.2.0` (commit path as of that release)
- Observed via source review (not a live exploit demo)

## Relevant code

1. Host request is queued from JS with the script-supplied URL string:

https://github.com/storytold/printcraft/blob/v0.2.0/crates/js/src/lib.rs

```rust
fn launch_url(_: &JsValue, args: &[JsValue], ctx: &mut Context) -> JsResult<JsValue> {
    let u = message(&arg(args, 0), "cURL", ctx)?;
    host(ctx)?.borrow_mut().requests.push(Request::LaunchUrl(u));
    Ok(JsValue::undefined())
}
```

(`app.launchURL` is registered on the `app` object in the same file.)

2. UI handles `Request::LaunchUrl` by opening the URL directly:

https://github.com/storytold/printcraft/blob/v0.2.0/crates/ui-egui/src/js_ui.rs

```rust
Request::LaunchUrl(u) => {
    if let Some(ctx) = &self.ctx {
        ctx.open_url(egui::OpenUrl::new_tab(u));
    }
}
```

3. JavaScript defaults to on:

https://github.com/storytold/printcraft/blob/v0.2.0/crates/engine/src/js.rs

```rust
/// Preferences ▸ JavaScript ▸ Enable Acrobat JavaScript (on by default).
pub fn set_javascript(&mut self, on: bool) {
```

The Preferences UI also states scripts run without network access, which conflicts with this path.

## Potential impact

- A crafted PDF can open `https://attacker.example/?data=...` (or other schemes) when the user interacts with form/button scripts that call `launchURL`.
- Values the user typed into PDF form fields may be included in that URL if the script reads them first.
- `submitForm` a…

title: PDF URI actions and button_script(app.launchURL) open URLs without confirmation (bypasses LaunchUrl-only fixes)
author: Harshith292002
body:
## Summary

Related to #90 (`Request::LaunchUrl` / `app.launchURL` via the JS request queue): **other PDF-origin paths open arbitrary URLs with `egui::OpenUrl` and have no confirmation or scheme allowlist.** A fix that only gates `Request::LaunchUrl` in `js_ui` would leave these open.

## Environment

- Tag: `v0.2.0` (`2ea5846a165c6a265533d0ecb2c8153415bb7606`)
- Source review only (not a live exploit demo)

## Paths

### 1. Link annotation click

https://github.com/storytold/printcraft/blob/v0.2.0/crates/ui-egui/src/canvas.rs

```rust
LinkTarget::Uri(u) => ui.ctx().open_url(egui::OpenUrl::new_tab(u))
```

### 2. Push-button `/A` URI action

Same file — button URI actions call `ctx.open_url(...)` similarly (`B::Uri`).

### 3. Explicit #90 bypass: `button_script` maps `app.launchURL` → URI

https://github.com/storytold/printcraft/blob/v0.2.0/crates/forms/src/af.rs

`button_script` recognizes one-liner `app.launchURL(...)` and maps it to `ButtonAction::Uri`, which then hits the canvas open path above — **not** `Request::LaunchUrl`.

### Shared helper

`PrintCraftApp::open_url` in `crates/ui-egui/src/lib.rs` also appears to lack scheme checks (used from help/update UI; PDF paths often call `ctx.open_url` directly).

## Impact

Same class as #90: click (or scripted button) can open `https://…` (possible exfil after interaction) or non-`https` schemes (`file:`, custom handlers) via the OS. Button URIs are easier to disguise than a visible link (links may show a hover URL).

## Suggested fix

One gated opener for **all PDF-origin URLs**:

1. Confirm with the full URL (default Deny)
2. Scheme allowlist (e.g. `https` / `http` / `mailto` per policy)
3. Route link clicks, `B::Uri`, and `Request::LaunchUrl` through that helper
4. Keep recognizing `app.launchURL` in `button_script` only if it still goes through the same gate

See also #90 for the JS `Request::LaunchUrl` path and default-on JavaScript / prefs copy mismatch.

title: Linux Wayland: default LowPower GPU preference causes startup failure on hybrid Intel/NVIDIA system
author: shangjung1012
body:
## Environment

- Linux, GNOME Wayland
- Intel UHD Graphics 770 (`i915`)
- NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5080
- NVIDIA driver: `580.178.04`
- `egui-wgpu`: `0.36.2`
- `wgpu`: `30.0.1`
- PrintCraft: current `main`

GNOME Shell is running on the NVIDIA GPU.

## Problem

PrintCraft fails to start with the default GPU configuration on this hybrid Intel/NVIDIA system.

Running:

```console
cargo run --release -p printcraft
```

fails with:

```text
[destroyed object]: error 7: failed to import supplied dmabufs:
Could not bind the given EGLImage to a CoglTexture2D

printcraft: internal error: panicked at .../egui-wgpu-0.36.2/src/winit.rs:129:18:
The surface isn't supported by this adapter

Protocol error 7 on object @0
```

The current `configure_gpu()` implementation defaults to the low-power adapter when `WGPU_POWER_PREF` is not set:

```rust
if std::env::var_os("WGPU_POWER_PREF").is_none() {
    setup.power_preference = eframe::wgpu::PowerPreference::LowPower;
}
```

On this machine, that default appears to result in selecting a GPU configuration that cannot present correctly to the current Wayland surface.

## Workaround

Explicitly requesting the high-performance GPU fixes the problem completely:

```console
WGPU_POWER_PREF=high cargo run --release -p printcraft
```

PrintCraft then starts and works normally.

Explicitly requesting NVIDIA through `WGPU_ADAPTER_NAME` did not fix it:

```console
WGPU_ADAPTER_NAME=NVIDIA cargo run --release -p printcraft
```

and explicitly using Vulkan also still failed:

```console
WGPU_ADAPTER_NAME="GeForce RTX 5080" \
WGPU_BACKEND=vulkan \
cargo run --release -p printcraft
```

with the same Wayland/dmabuf and unsupported-surface errors.

Using the GL backend was not available for this surface:

```text
RequestAdapterError(NotFound {
    ...
    incompatible_surface_backends: Backends(GL)
})
```

## Possible regression from #31 / #8

I noticed that the low-power preference was introduced to address #8, where using the discrete NVIDIA GPU caused…

title: Render: fractional page sizes are truncated, so the last partial row and column of the page are lost (A4 at 72 dpi → 595×841)
author: EthanSuquet
body:
**Version:** printcraft-cli, main @ 55c5817 · macOS 26 (Darwin 25.6), Apple M2 Max, release build · hayro 0.7.1

### What happens

`printcraft-cli render a4.pdf --page 1 --dpi 72 --out p.pam` gives a 595×841 image for an A4 page
(595.28×841.89 pt). Poppler (`pdftoppm -r 72`) gives 596×842, macOS ColorSync 595×842. The bottom
0.89 px of the page is never drawn. It happens at every resolution whenever the scaled page size is not a
whole number (at 300 dpi A4 is 2480.3×3507.9 px and renders as 2480×3507), so content touching the bottom
or right edge (bleeds, full-page backgrounds, footers drawn to the edge) loses its last partial pixel row
or column. Other pages that are not whole points behave the same (e.g. a 1194.5 pt wide spread → 1194 px).

### Cause

`crates/render/src/raster.rs` (`render_page`, the untiled branch) passes `RenderSettings` without a
width/height, and hayro 0.7.1 then uses `scaled_width.floor()` / `scaled_height.floor()`
(`hayro/src/lib.rs:128-131`).

### Repro (synthetic)

Any one-page PDF with `/MediaBox [0 0 595.28 841.89]` and a full-page fill, e.g. a content stream
`0 0 1 rg 0 0 595.28 841.89 re f`:

```
printcraft-cli render a4.pdf --page 1 --dpi 72 --out p.pam   # 595×841
pdftoppm -r 72 -png a4.pdf p                                  # 596×842
```

**Expected:** the raster covers the whole page box (round up, as poppler does), with the partial edge
pixels anti-aliased against the page background. **Actual:** the size is rounded down.

### Suggested fix

Pass `width: Some(ceil(w × scale))`, `height: Some(ceil(h × scale))` (clamped as `effective_scale` already
does) in the untiled branch, and keep tile sizes in step.

Low priority: one pixel row at most, but it shows up as a size mismatch against every other renderer.

title: page_add_text, doc_header_footer and doc_watermark replace Japanese characters with "?" and report success
author: htdtkshi
body:
## Summary
Via the MCP server, `page_add_text`, `doc_header_footer` and `doc_watermark` accept Japanese text without an error, but the saved PDF contains `?` in place of every Japanese character (the watermark renders as a large "???"). The tool descriptions list only `helvetica/times/courier` for `font`, so I understand Latin-only output may be intended, but the call returns success with no warning.

## Environment
- Linux x86_64 (Ubuntu, headless Codespace), printcraft 0.2.1 (`printcraft-cli mcp`, tools/list = 123 tools)
- poppler `pdftotext` / `pdffonts` used to inspect output

## Steps to reproduce
Drive `printcraft-cli mcp` over stdio (JSON-RPC, protocol 2025-06-18) with a one-page PDF:

3. `doc_header_footer {"doc":1,"footer_center":"はただ商店"}`
4. `doc_watermark {"doc":1,"text":"社外秘"}`
5. `doc_save {"doc":1,"path":"jp-edit.pdf"}`
6. `pdftotext -layout jp-edit.pdf -` ; `pdffonts jp-edit.pdf`

## Expected
Either the Japanese text is written (with an embedded CJK-capable font), or the tool returns an error/warning that the characters cannot be encoded.

## Actual
All three calls return success. `pdftotext` shows `??????: ????? 10?22???` for the body text and `?????` for the footer; `pdffonts` lists only Helvetica (WinAnsiEncoding) for the added text. The watermark is drawn as "???". The watermark is visible as "???" when the page is rendered.

## Notes
- Reproduced n=2 (identical output both runs). `comment_add` (note, highlight) with Japanese text was also sent in the same script; I did not separately verify how the note contents are stored.
- Duplicate check (storytold/printcraft, --state all): "page_add_text", "watermark", "header_footer", "unicode", "non-ASCII", "CJK", "日本語", "Helvetica", "WinAnsi", "font" -> no matching Issue. Loosely related: #34 (closed, currency symbols in form text).

title: text_find does not return occurrences in vertically laid-out text
author: htdtkshi
body:
## Summary
In a PDF that contains the same string once horizontally and once vertically (one glyph per line, top to bottom), `text_find` returns only the horizontal occurrence.

## Environment
- Linux x86_64 (Ubuntu, headless), printcraft 0.2.1, `printcraft-cli mcp`
- Test PDF made with reportlab (non-embedded CID font, one character drawn per line for the vertical column); `pdftotext` extracts both occurrences.

3. MCP: `doc_open {"path":"vert.pdf"}`, then `text_find {"doc":1,"query":"商店"}`.

## Expected
`count` = 2 (horizontal and vertical).

## Actual
`count` = 1; the single rect is on the horizontal line (y ≈ 45.9). Same for `はただ商店` (1), `セール` (1), `10月22日` (1).

## Notes
- n=2 per query, 4 queries.
- Duplicate check (storytold/printcraft, --state all): "text_find", "find vertical", "tategaki", "CJK", "日本語", "text extraction" -> none.

## Script to generate vert.pdf
```python

from reportlab.pdfbase import pdfmetrics
from reportlab.pdfbase.cidfonts import CIDFont
f=CIDFont('HeiseiMin-W3','UniJIS-UCS2-V'); pdfmetrics.registerFont(f); VN=f.fontName

title: fix(automation): --root refusals reveal whether paths outside the root exist
author: coygeek
body:
## Summary

With `--root DIR`, `printcraft-cli run` and `printcraft-cli mcp` refuse paths outside `DIR`, but the error text depends on whether the outside path exists. An existing outside file or directory is refused with `<path> is outside the allowed directory <root>`. A missing outside path fails with `<path>: No such file or directory (os error 2)`, and a path below an existing outside file fails with `<path>: Not a directory (os error 20)`. A client confined to the root, such as an MCP agent, can therefore test whether files and directories outside the root exist, and tell files from directories, with one tool call per probe. Writing tools show a narrower variant of the same difference. No file contents are read and no file is written outside the root.

title: fix(cli): script PNG output paths bypass --root confinement
author: coygeek
body:
## Summary

`printcraft-cli run --script steps.json --root DIR` writes each step's rendered PNG to the step's `"out"` path without applying the `--root` confinement that tool paths receive. An absolute `"out"` path outside the root creates or replaces that file. A relative `"out"` path resolves against the process working directory instead of the root. A tool-side write to the same outside directory under the same root is correctly rejected. A user who runs a script written by someone else under `--root` can therefore have files outside the root created or overwritten with PNG data, within the process's own filesystem permissions.

## Runtime or environment

Runtime reproduction used the official macOS universal CLI release v0.2.1, tag commit `dcb00238896e418b357e6dd777ee35bad36f0b97`, on macOS 27.0.1, Darwin 27.0.0, arm64. The release zip's SHA-256 was `bda65829033916c5de5a7ddc0763437f8db2e8792ee43c8dc2676434acb3d495`, matching the release's `SHA256SUMS.txt`. The extracted binary's SHA-256 was `b7783b596870ed5a326f29456d4647382d2e1e4d7b7ffe75ded192cd15b86995`, and `--version` reported `printcraft-cli 0.2.1`.

The default branch was inspected at `1c78ff479ce5cf5cbcf7af5100378c9311b95162`. `git diff v0.2.1 origin/main -- apps/printcraft-cli crates/automation` changes only `forms.rs`, `tools.rs`, the automation README's status and MCP text, and an automation test. The CLI's `run` and `print_output` and `Automation::resolve` are unchanged. The branch was not built or executed; runtime observations below are from the release binary.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Put the release binary on `PATH` as `printcraft-cli`. Python 3 is used only to write a synthetic one-page PDF.

### Environment

quick fix in the installer definition.

title: Edit text: a line whose `TJ` operands end one content stream and whose operator starts the next can't be selected or edited
author: EthanSuquet
body:
**Version:** printcraft-cli, main @ 1c78ff4 · macOS 26.6 (Darwin 25.6), Apple M2 Max, release build

### What happens

A page's `/Contents` array is one content stream in pieces, and writers may split it between any two
tokens (ISO 32000-2 §7.8.2). Several office and layout exporters split right between a `TJ` array and
its `TJ` operator. Text extraction and rendering handle this, but Edit text does not: `text_lines`
(and so `text_paragraphs` / `text_edit` and the Edit text tool in the app) parses each piece on its
own, so the operator arrives with no operands and the line is never listed. It can't be selected,
retyped or restyled.

### Repro (synthetic)

One page, `/Contents [4 0 R 5 0 R 6 0 R]`, font `/F1` = Helvetica (WinAnsi):

```
4: /P << /MCID 0
5: >> BDC BT /F1 12 Tf 72 700 Td (Target) Tj 0 -20 Td [(After) -20 (wards)]
6: TJ ET EMC
```

```
printcraft-cli text split.pdf                         # Target / Afterwards
printcraft-cli run --script s.json                    # text_lines → only "Target"
```

with `s.json` = `[{"tool":"doc_open","args":{"path":"split.pdf"}},{"tool":"text_lines","args":{"doc":1,"page":1}}]`.

**Expected:** `text_lines` lists "Target" and "Afterwards". **Actual:** only "Target"; "Afterwards" is
not editable.

### Cause

`crates/edit/src/text.rs`, `text_lines`: `for (si, (_, data)) in content_streams(...) { let ops = parse(&data).ops; … }`.
`printcraft_content::parse` drops operands left at the end of a piece (they are counted in
`Parsed::skipped`). The redaction interpreter had the same problem; the fix there parses the pieces
joined and gives each operator back to the piece its keyword is in (#153).
#150 already threads the graphics state between pieces in
`interpret`; threading the pending operands (or parsing the joined pieces) would complete it.

`crates/edit/src/images.rs` (Edit ▸ image move/replace/delete) parses and re-serializes one piece
the same way, so it probably drops a split operator's operands too (not verified).

Found…

title: [Bug] Browser Print Save as PDF closes without output or explanation
author: Jagalite
body:
The browser Print dialog offers an enabled Save as PDF action, but clicking it closes the dialog without downloading the print-layout PDF or explaining that the action is unavailable.

## Environment

- Updated `main`: `1c78ff479ce5cf5cbcf7af5100378c9311b95162`, freshly rebuilt release browser bundle and verified against the remote on 2026-10-07.
- macOS 26.5.2 arm64; Rust 1.95.0, wasm-bindgen 0.2.129.
- Isolated headless Chrome 154.0.8037.93, Firefox 155.0 and Playwright WebKit 26.6 (not Safari), 1280×800.

## Steps

1. Open a generated three-page PDF containing ordinary standard-14 text and simple colored rectangles.
2. Press Ctrl+S: an ordinary PDF download succeeds and independently contains all three pages.
3. Press Ctrl+P. Select Multiple page handling, with two pages per sheet.
4. Leave Printer set to Save as PDF and click the enabled Save as PDF button.

Expected: download the PDF shown by the print preview, or give a clear unavailable-action explanation.

Actual in all three browsers: the preview correctly shows two pages on the first sheet. Clicking Save as PDF closes the dialog and returns to the editor. No new download appears during five visible seconds and there is no visible error or capability explanation. There is no page exception. The healthy ordinary Save download works in the same context.

One actual dialog reproduction per browser; before/after screenshots were reviewed. No file-read fault or response injection was used. This concerns generating a print-layout PDF, not physical printers or native GUI printing.

In `crates/ui-egui/src/print_ui.rs`, `print_now` generates the print PDF but the Wasm `None` save destination resolves to `None`, then returns `false` without notifying the user. A browser download path or explicit disabled/unavailable UI is needed.

title: MacOS - PrintCraft greyed out in Open With, forced open says it cannot open PDF files
author: ShauryaSwarup
body:
Follow-up to #73.

On macOS 27.0 (Golden Gate), seen with the v0.2.1 release DMG (`printcraft-0.2.1-macos-universal.dmg` — installed PrintCraft.app reports 0.2.1, build `dcb0023`) and current `main`, right-clicking a PDF > Open With does not list PrintCraft under Recommended Applications — it is greyed out, and I have to switch `Enable: Recommended Applications` to `Enable: All Applications` to pick it. Opening it that way then fails with:

> The document "xyz.pdf" could not be opened. PrintCraft cannot open files in the "PDF document" format.

What I found while digging: `packaging/macos/Info.plist.in` declares the PDF document type by extension (`pdf`) and MIME type (`application/pdf`) only, with no `LSItemContentTypes`. Checking with `lsregister -dump`, the app's claim comes out as `bindings: .pdf, application/pdf` instead of `bindings: com.adobe.pdf` the way the system's PDF handlers declare it, so Finder never treats it as a recommended PDF app.

Declaring `LSItemContentTypes: com.adobe.pdf` (keeping extension + MIME for compatibility) makes the claim resolve to `com.adobe.pdf` with rank Alternate / role Editor. PR with the fix: #176.

body:

On Windows, **Use a certificate ▸ Digitally sign** offers a .p12/.pfx file or a new self-signed ID. title: [Bug] Checkboxes with an indirect /AP /N state dictionary are not drawn
author: ebastos
body:
Checkboxes and radio buttons whose normal appearance (`/AP /N`) is an **indirect dictionary** of states are not drawn. The same dictionary written inline still draws. Quartz writes the indirect form when it saves a checkbox, so the widget disappears while the rest of the page looks complete.

This is separate from #152 (clicking to fill a box) and #94 (checkbox styles). The appearances in this file already exist.

## Environment

- `main` at `d3db99818f533a531dbcd469b2ac71ba35c0d3ec`.
- On that commit, `parse_fallback` in `vendor/hayro-syntax/src/object/stream.rs` still searches the rest of the file for the bytes `stream`, and `vendor/hayro-interpret/src/interpret/mod.rs` still reads `/N` with `get::<Stream>` before trying the state dictionary.
- The pictures below are from a debug build of `1c78ff4` with that same unpatched function, then with the fix. rustc 1.99.0, macOS 26.6.1 arm64.

## Steps

1. Generate the fixture with the script at the bottom. It writes `indirect-appearance-state-checkbox.pdf` (3100 bytes, sha256 `7e724c9d22413243d6b60a39a9b9108844bdb7ac297bbebc089131a6b17bf467`). One page, no personal data. The words use the standard Helvetica name. The boxes are path drawings.
2. Open the file.

title: [BUG] Render: Images exported as PDFs are opened and displayed warped
author: philkwek
body:
## Summary

Image-only PDFs produced by jsPDF render at a much smaller scale in PrintCraft than in Chrome/Preview. The page itself is correct, but the page image occupies only a narrow central portion of it, leaving large white margins.

## Environment

- PrintCraft: Version 0.2.1
- macOS on Apple Silicon
- PDF producer: jsPDF 3.0.3
- Comparison viewer: Google Chrome (renders correctly)

## Expected behaviour

The embedded page image should be scaled to fill the page according to the PDF content stream's current transformation matrix (CTM), as it is in other PDF viewers such as Chrome or Preview (Tested on a mac).

## Actual behaviour

PrintCraft appears to render the embedded JPEG close to its intrinsic size instead of applying the full page-scale transform. Text and other content therefore look severely horizontally compressed / shrunken within an otherwise oversized white page.

## Investigation

The issue appears to be in the rendering path rather than PDF opening or view zoom:

- `crates/render/src/raster.rs` sends the page to the renderer.
- `vendor/hayro-interpret/src/x_object.rs` handles image XObjects and builds their transform.
- `vendor/hayro/src/renderer.rs` rasterises the transformed image.

The unusually large page also triggers PrintCraft's large-page tiling path, so that path may contribute. The CTM/Image-XObject interaction is the primary suspected cause; this has not yet been isolated to a specific line.

## Reproduction

1. Create an image-only PDF with jsPDF 3.0.3: use a non-personal JPEG page image and place it at `(0, 0)` at the full jsPDF page size.
2. Open the PDF in Chrome and PrintCraft side by side.
3. Chrome shows the image filling the page; PrintCraft shows a narrow/shrunken image inside a much larger white page.

## Notes
- This is distinct from #102, which concerns one-pixel rounding at fractional page dimensions rather than an image placement scale mismatch.

title: doc_split copies every image from the source document into each part (each part ≈ full size)
author: ChippedW
body:
## Description

Splitting a large PDF puts all the images of the source document into every output part, even the images its pages never draw. Each part ends up nearly as large as the whole original. `doc_optimize` doesn't remove these images, and `doc_reduce` barely helps.

## Steps to reproduce

1. `doc_open` a 9,445-page PDF (186 MB; ~2,900 images, all pages share one resource dictionary)
2. `doc_split` with `every: 1500` → 7 parts
3. Each part is 104–110 MB; together they total ~755 MB, versus 186 MB for the source

## Analysis (part 1, pages 1–1500)

| | Image XObjects | Image bytes | File size |
|---|---|---|---|
| Source (9,445 p.) | 2,889 | 106 MB | 186 MB |
| Part 1 (1,500 p.) | 2,908 | 106 MB | 116 MB |

`doc_optimize` reports `images: 304` (the images part 1 actually draws), yet all ~2,900 are still embedded. They are still listed in the shared `/Resources /XObject` dictionary, so nothing treats them as unreferenced.

- `doc_optimize` (lossless: `compression: retain`, no downsampling): 115,671,511 → 115,669,977 bytes (no real change)
- `doc_reduce`: −2.6 %, and it recompresses images with loss

## Expected

`doc_split` / `page_extract` should keep only the resources each part's pages actually use (like qpdf's `--remove-unreferenced-resources`). At the very least, `doc_optimize` should remove XObjects that are listed but never drawn.

## Environment

- Windows 11 Pro (10.0.26200)
- PrintCraft version: 0.2.1
- Used via the MCP server

title: CJK glyphs in PDFs without an embedded CJK font render as .notdef boxes (□)
author: ZhouZG-Gaogle
body:
e hi devs，PdfCraft never overrides hayro's `font_resolver`, so the default implementation
is always in effect:
1. `crates/render/src/raster.rs:51-55` — `RenderConfig::settings()` builds its
   settings with `..InterpreterSettings::default()` and therefore inherits the
   default resolver.
2. `vendor/hayro-interpret/src/interpret/mod.rs:117-121` — the default resolver
   answers a `FontQuery::Fallback` with `pick_standard_font()` only, which can
   return nothing beyond the 14 PDF standard fonts.
3. The fonts actually embedded for that path live in
   `vendor/hayro-interpret/assets/`. Decoding their CFF tables shows the
   coverage:
   | Font        | Glyphs | `/Encoding` codes | Codes > 0xFF |
   |-------------|--------|-------------------|--------------|
   | FoxitSans   |    230 |                 0 |            0 |
   | FoxitSerif  |    230 |                 0 |            0 |
   | FoxitFixed  |    244 |                 0 |            0 |
   230 glyphs is a Latin-only character set. Han characters live in
   U+4E00–U+9FFF; these fonts contain none of them.
4. `vendor/hayro-interpret/src/font/true_type.rs:367` — `map_code` returns
   `GlyphId::NOTDEF` when no glyph is found.
5. `vendor/hayro-interpret/src/font/standard_font.rs:336-341` — `NOTDEF` is
   rendered from the font's own `.notdef` outline. The comment there notes that
   in Liberation Sans this is a rectangle, which is the box the user sees.
Searching `crates/` for `load_system_fonts`, `fontdb` or `FallbackProvider`
returns nothing: the rendering pipeline never queries the OS font directory, so
SimSun, Microsoft YaHei and friends are never considered.

title: [Bug] pdfcraft-cli render --out file.png writes a Netpbm PAM file (P7), not a PNG
author: samfareed
body:
## Bug Description

`pdfcraft-cli render --out <name>.png` writes a **Netpbm PAM** file (P7 magic) but names it `.png`. The output cannot be opened as a PNG by any image library or viewer.

## Steps to Reproduce

```
printcraft-cli render "101-linux-commands-light.pdf" --page 1 --out p1.png
```

Output on stdout:

```
rendered page 1 at 96 dpi: 793x1122 px in 64 ms
```

The file `p1.png` was created, but its contents are not a PNG. The first bytes are:

```
P7
WIDTH 793
HEIGHT 1122
DEPTH 4
MAXVAL 255
TUPLTYPE RGB_ALPHA
ENDHDR
```

## Actual Behavior

- `file p1.png` reports: `Netpbm PAM image file, size = 793 x 1122`
- Pillow: `PIL.UnidentifiedImageError: cannot identify image file 'p1.png'`
- Any image viewer that trusts the `.png` extension fails to open it.

The PAM data itself is correct (RGBA, the right dimensions, contents render properly once read as PAM).

## Expected Behavior

Either write a valid PNG when the caller asks for `.png`, or honour the requested extension / write a `.pam` file and say so. A file named `.png` should be a PNG.

## Environment

- OS: Windows 11 (x64)
- Version: `printcraft-cli 0.2.1` from the Windows x64 portable build in the v0.2.1 release (binary is `printcraft-cli.exe`)
- Also reproducible via the `render` tool in the JSON tool catalogue.

title: [Bug] pdfcraft-cli split --out-dir fails when the directory does not exist (os error 3)
author: samfareed
body:
## Bug Description

`pdfcraft-cli split --out-dir <dir>` fails if `<dir>` does not already exist. It does not create the output directory, and reports a filesystem error instead of producing parts.

## Steps to Reproduce

```
printcraft-cli split "101-linux-commands-light.pdf" --every 300 --out-dir "C:\work\parts"
```

where `C:\work\parts` does not exist yet.

## Actual Behavior

```
printcraft-cli: C:\work\parts\101-linux-commands-light-p1-300.pdf: The system cannot find the path specified. (os error 3)
```

No files are written. The same command succeeds once the directory is created manually:

```
mkdir "C:\work\parts"
printcraft-cli split "101-linux-commands-light.pdf" --every 300 --out-dir "C:\work\parts"
# -> 101-linux-commands-light-p1-300.pdf, ...-p301-600.pdf, ...-p601-900.pdf, ...-p901-1032.pdf
```

## Expected Behavior

`--out-dir` should create the directory if missing (create_dir_all), or print a clear message saying the directory must already exist. Failing with a raw `os error 3` after the user supplied an output folder is easy to misread as a failure of the split itself.

title: Full Arabic/RTL Support and Automatic System Font Discovery
author: A7madabdo
body:
PdfCraft would benefit from improved support for Arabic and other RTL/complex scripts, together with automatic detection of all fonts installed on the user's operating system.

The goal is to allow users to create, edit, render, search, copy, and extract Arabic text correctly without manually installing or configuring fonts inside PdfCraft.

1. Full Arabic / RTL Support

Arabic text should correctly support:

Right-to-left (RTL) layout
Unicode Bidirectional Algorithm (UAX #9)
Arabic contextual glyph shaping
Connected Arabic characters
Correct character joining
Correct text direction
Mixed Arabic and English text
Mixed Arabic and numbers
Arabic-Indic numbers
Correct cursor movement
Correct text selection
Correct copy/paste
Arabic text search
Correct PDF text extraction

For example:

مرحبا بالعالم

هذا نص عربي لاختبار دعم اللغة العربية.

مرحبا World 123

السعر: ١٢٣ ريال

The logical Unicode order should be preserved internally while the text is rendered visually in the correct RTL direction.

2. Automatically Detect All System Fonts

PdfCraft should automatically discover fonts installed on the user's operating system instead of requiring users to manually provide fonts.

Windows

Detect fonts from locations such as:

C:\Windows\Fonts
User-installed fonts
Linux

Detect fonts from locations such as:

/usr/share/fonts
/usr/local/share/fonts
~/.local/share/fonts
macOS

Detect fonts from:

/System/Library/Fonts
/Library/Fonts
~/Library/Fonts

The application should automatically build and maintain a font registry.

A font installed on the operating system should become available in PdfCraft without requiring the user to copy it into a PdfCraft-specific directory.

3. Font Metadata

The font system should detect and expose:

Font family
Font name
Font style
Font weight
Bold/italic variants
Unicode coverage
Script/language coverage
Font file location/identifier

For example:

Arial
Arial Bold
Arial Italic
Tahoma
Noto Sans Arabic
Noto Naskh Arabic
Amiri
DejaVu Sans

title: fix(automation): comment_add puts a note or attachment icon one icon-width off on rotated pages
author: wstock
body:
## Summary

`comment_add` documents `at` for `note` as "[x, y] (icon top-left)" and for `attachment` as "its icon's top-left", in the automation convention (points from the top-left of the displayed page). On a page with `/Rotate 90`, `180` or `270` the icon is placed one icon width (20 pt) away from that point along one or both axes; `comment_list` then reports a rectangle that does not start at `at`. Unrotated pages are correct.

## Steps to reproduce

```
doc_create  { "from": "blank", "width": 612, "height": 792, "pages": 2 }
page_rotate { "doc": D, "pages": [2], "degrees": 90 }
comment_add { "doc": D, "page": 1, "type": "note", "at": [72, 72], "contents": "x" }
comment_add { "doc": D, "page": 2, "type": "note", "at": [72, 72], "contents": "x" }
comment_list { "doc": D }
```

## Expected

Both notes report `rect: [72, 72, 92, 92]` — a 20 pt square whose displayed top-left is the requested point, as on page 1.

## Actual

Page 1: `[72, 72, 92, 92]`. Page 2: `[52, 72, 72, 92]` — the icon sits 20 pt to the left of the requested point. With `degrees: 180` it is off by 20 pt in both axes, with `270` by 20 pt in y. `type: "attachment"` behaves the same (`at: [200, 300]` on the 90° page gives `[180, 300, 200, 320]`).

## Cause

`crates/automation/src/comments.rs` converts `at` with `to_user` (a single point through `PageInfo::view_to_user`) and hands it to `Shape::Note { at }` / `Shape::Attachment { at }`. `rect_for` in `crates/annot/src/lib.rs` then builds `/Rect` as `[at.x, at.y - NOTE_SIZE, at.x + NOTE_SIZE, at.y]`, i.e. `at` is the **user-space** top-left of the icon square. On an unrotated page the displayed top-left and the user-space top-left are the same corner; under `/Rotate` they are different corners of the square, so the square extends from `at` in the wrong direction as displayed.

Noticed while fixing #129 (PR #242): its test asserts the note rectangle on the unrotated page only.

title: combine, extract and split drop /OutputIntents and the PDF/X identification
author: director-LAC
body:
Combining, extracting or splitting pages of a PDF/X-4 file writes a file with no `/OutputIntents` in the catalog, no `GTS_PDFXVersion` in Info and no `pdfxid` in the XMP. Page boxes, Separations and embedded fonts survive, and page content streams compare identical after normalising, so the artwork is untouched. The output just stops being PDF/X, and a downstream RIP or preflight loses the intended output condition.

**Repro** (pdfcraft-cli 0.3.0, main @ ed2e349; same on 0.2.1)
1. Make a PDF/X-4 with designcraft-cli (main): a 3.5 x 2 in document with 9 pt bleed, any content, then `file.exportPdf {"path": "card.pdf", "bleed": true, "standard": "x4"}`
2. `pdfcraft-cli combine card.pdf card.pdf --out combined.pdf`
3. `pdfcraft-cli extract card.pdf --pages 1 --out extracted.pdf`
4. `pdfcraft-cli split two-page-x4.pdf --every 1 --out-dir parts` (the card twice)

| file | OutputIntents | GTS_PDFXVersion | XMP pdfxid | TrimBox |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| card.pdf | 1 | PDF/X-4 | yes | 33 33 285 177 |
| combined.pdf | 0 | none | no | 33 33 285 177 |
| extracted.pdf | 0 | none | no | 33 33 285 177 |
| parts/*-p1.pdf, *-p2.pdf | 0 | none | no | 33 33 285 177 |

**Likely cause:** `crates/organize/src/import.rs` carries Names, OCProperties, AcroForm, Outlines and PageLabels into the new document; nothing copies the catalog's `/OutputIntents` or `/Metadata`. OutputIntents is only handled in `crates/preflight`.

**Suggested behaviour**
- Extract and split from one source: carry the source's `/OutputIntents` over.
- Combine: carry them over when every source has the same output intent (same OutputConditionIdentifier and profile bytes); when they differ or some sources have none, keep the first and report a warning.
- If dropping the PDF/X claim is deliberate, because conformance can't be guaranteed after editing, a warning like "output is no longer PDF/X" would make that visible.

Context: we're a commercial print shop testing the Crafting Apps as an agent-driven prepress toolchain.…

title: Feature request: open files in the running window as tabs (single instance)
author: anmacmillan
body:
PrintCraft 0.2.1 (build `dcb0023`), macOS 26, universal DMG.

### What happens

Every launch that carries a file starts a separate process with its own window. Open three PDFs one after another from a script and there are three copies of PrintCraft running, each with one tab:

```
open -n -a PrintCraft --args /path/one.pdf
open -n -a PrintCraft --args /path/two.pdf
/Applications/PrintCraft.app/Contents/MacOS/PrintCraft /path/three.pdf
```

After a morning of generating documents I had eight copies open. The only way to get tabs from outside the app is to quit it and relaunch once with every path on the command line, which loses unsaved changes and scroll positions.

### What I would like

If PrintCraft is already running, a second launch with file arguments hands those files to the running window, where they open as tabs, and then exits. A `--new-window` flag (or a setting) for anyone who wants the present behaviour.

### How this relates to #73

#82 fixes the Finder, Open With and Dock routes on macOS: the running app receives the open-documents event and opens the file as File ▸ Open does. That covers `open -a PrintCraft file.pdf` once it ships (0.2.1 does not have it). It does not cover:

- the binary launched with paths as arguments, or `open -n`, on macOS;
- Windows and Linux, where a file association launches the executable with the path, so each double-click in the file manager is presumably a new process and a new window.

A single-instance hand-off (a local socket or named pipe, checked at startup before the window is created) would close all three routes with one mechanism.

### Why it matters

Tabs are the reason to use one viewer for a set of related documents. Build tools, scripts and file managers all open files by launching the program with a path, and at present each of those is a new window.

title: Redact: partly covered JPEG, JPX, JBIG2 and CCITT images are removed whole, so one mark blanks a scanned page
author: anmacmillan
body:
Read from `crates/redact/README.md` and `crates/redact/src/image.rs` on `main`; installed version is 0.2.1 (build `dcb0023`), macOS.

### What happens

When a redaction mark partly covers an image, the result depends on how the image is compressed:

- Flate, LZW, RunLength, ASCII85, ASCIIHex: a copy is written with the covered pixels cleared. Correct.
- DCT (JPEG), JPX, JBIG2, CCITT: the whole image is removed.
- Any image over 64 megapixels: the whole image is removed.

The README lists this under "Not yet: re-encoding of DCT images (they are removed instead)".

Failing closed is the right default, and nothing leaks. But a scanned document is one full-page image per page, almost always DCT, JBIG2 or CCITT. Marking a single line on a scanned page (a name, an address, an account number) removes the entire page. The same goes for a photograph or a screenshot embedded as a JPEG: redact one face or one line of a message and the whole exhibit goes.

For disclosure and court bundles that is most of the redaction work. The material is scanned correspondence, medical records and photographs, and the task is to take out one detail and leave the rest of the page legible.

### What I would like

For a partly covered DCT, JPX, JBIG2 or CCITT image: decode it, clear the covered pixels as `image.rs` already does for Flate images, and write the result back.

- The renderer has to decode these codecs to draw the page, so the decode side should already exist.
- Writing the cleared copy as Flate needs no new encoder and is lossless. The file grows; that is an acceptable price for a correct redaction, and Optimize can deal with size afterwards.
- Re-encoding as JPEG (DCT) or CCITT G4 (bilevel) would keep files small. The covered samples are zeroed before encoding, so nothing of the original survives in the new stream.
- Soft masks (`/SMask`) and `/Mask` on the image need the same region cleared or left consistent.
- Keep removal as the fallback where an image cannot be decoded, so the…

### Summary

**Export to Word…** writes a `.docx` with no text and no images when a page's content is

title: UI tests: fill_sign sometimes crashes with an access violation when the image-signature tests share a process
author: pauliusiv123-rgb
body:
## What happens

On Windows, the `fill_sign` UI test binary (`crates/ui-egui/tests/fill_sign.rs`) sometimes dies with `STATUS_ACCESS_VIOLATION`, so `cargo test --workspace` fails even though no test reports a failure:

```
error: test failed, to rerun pass `-p pdfcraft-ui-egui --test fill_sign`

Caused by:
  process didn't exit successfully: `...\target\debug\deps\fill_sign-....exe` (exit code: 0xc0000005, STATUS_ACCESS_VIOLATION)
```

In the run above it died after 9 of the 11 tests had reported `ok`.

## How often

Test binary built from main at b5edb59 and run directly (default test threads unless noted):

| Tests in the process | Crashes |
|---|---|
| all 11 | 3/30 (an earlier batch: 4/20) |
| the 4 `image_*` tests only | 3/30 |
| the other 7 tests | 0/30 |
| each `image_*` test alone | 0/25 each |
| `image_signature_preview_follows_pointer_at_page_size_with_zoom_and_rotation` + `image_signature_placement_selects_resize_handles_and_requires_reselecting_to_repeat` | 2/25 |
| the other five pairs of `image_*` tests | 0/25 each |
| all 11 with `--test-threads=1` | 1/10, then 0/20 |

So it needs at least two of the image-signature tests from #335 in one process, and running them in parallel makes it much more likely.

## Possible cause

This looks like the crash #71 fixed in `view.rs`: two tests rendering pixels at once, each on its own wgpu device. Both tests in the crashing pair call `Harness::render()` (directly or through `rendered_ink`), and #335 added them without the `GPU` mutex that `view.rs` takes before rendering. `fill_sign.rs` has no such lock. I'll open a PR that takes the same lock in those tests. The lock changes nothing with one test thread, so the single-threaded crash (1 in 30) may have another cause.

CI hasn't caught it so far: the extended file has run about eight times since #335, all passing, which isn't unlikely at a 1-in-5 rate.

## To reproduce

```
cargo test -p pdfcraft-ui-egui --test fill_sign --no-run
```

Then run the binary it prints …

author: jcl-bit
body:
I tested the 0.4.0 macOS DMG on macOS 27.0.1 (Apple Silicon) before deploying it to client Macs. The signing and notarization are good. One thing trips the checks an MSP or MDM script usually runs.

### What works

- `pdfcraft-0.4.0-macos-universal.dmg` matches `SHA256SUMS.txt` (`740da490…fa10`).
- The DMG and `PdfCraft.app` are Developer ID signed (team `DJ6XS33FX8`), hardened runtime, timestamped, notarized, and the ticket is stapled to both (`xcrun stapler validate` passes).
- `spctl -a -t open --context context:primary-signature` on the DMG and `spctl --assess --type execute` on the app both say `accepted, source=Notarized Developer ID`, with and without a `com.apple.quarantine` flag.
- `hdiutil attach -nobrowse -readonly` mounts it, with and without quarantine. (So does the exact `printcraft-0.2.1` image from #117; more on that below.)

### The problem

`codesign --verify --strict` rejects the app, both inside the mounted DMG and after it is copied into `/Applications` with `ditto`:

```
$ hdiutil attach -nobrowse -readonly -mountpoint ./mnt pdfcraft-0.4.0-macos-universal.dmg
$ codesign --verify --deep --strict --verbose=2 mnt/PdfCraft.app

title: [Feature Request] Add Restore Sessions
author: naymata
body:
**Description**

_It would be great to have a feature that allows users to restore their previous PDF sessions when reopening the application, similar to the session recovery functionality available in Adobe Acrobat Reader._

**Proposed Feature**

- **Restore previous sessions:** _Automatically restore the PDFs that were open during the previous session when the application is launched again._
- **Restore reading position:** _Remember the last viewed page for each PDF and return users to that page when the document is reopened._
- **Restore multiple documents:** _If multiple PDFs were open when the application was closed, allow users to restore all previously open documents._
- **Remember session state:** _Preserve relevant reading settings, such as zoom level, page layout, and scroll position, wherever possible._
- **Session recovery:** _If the application closes unexpectedly or crashes, offer users the option to restore their previous session on the next launch._
- **User control:** _Allow users to enable or disable session restoration through the application settings, and provide an option to start a fresh session instead._

**Use Case**

- _When working with multiple PDF documents, users often need to close the application or restart their computer and later continue where they left off. Currently, they may have to reopen each document manually and navigate back to the page they were reading._
- _A built-in session restoration feature would make the workflow more convenient and efficient by allowing users to resume their work without losing their place or reopening documents one by one._


**Additional Notes**

_Ideally, the feature should support both normal application restarts and recovery after unexpected shutdowns. It should remember previously opened documents and their individual reading positions, while giving users control over whether sessions are restored automatically._

**Thanks for considering this feature!**

title: Web build: an embedding API to open and save PDFs from the host page
author: wangbingjie1
body:
### What
The same idea as FilmCraft's `window.filmcraft`: let a page that embeds the PdfCraft web build hand it a PDF and get the edited PDF back.

### Why
We drive PdfCraft headless through `pdfcraft-cli mcp` in an AI agent's sandbox and want people to review and adjust the result in the web build. `?file=<url>` (`apps/pdfcraft-web/src/main.rs`) covers opening when the PDF has a CORS-enabled URL, but there is no way to open bytes the host already has, and saving always goes to a browser download, so the host never sees the edited file.

### Proposal
- `open(bytes, name)` from an ArrayBuffer.
- `save()` returning the PDF bytes (optionally a page PNG) to the caller.
- A change notification (an event or `isDirty()`).
- `window.pdfcraft`, plus a `postMessage` mirror for cross-origin iframes with an allowed parent origin.

A sibling request for PhotoCraft: storytold/photocraft#1614

title: Release: a standalone Linux CLI archive
author: wangbingjie1
body:
### What
Publish `pdfcraft-cli-<version>-linux-x86_64.tar.gz` (and aarch64) next to the existing `pdfcraft-cli-<version>-macos-universal.zip`, listed in `SHA256SUMS.txt`.

### Why
On Linux the CLI ships only inside the desktop packages (`packaging/linux/package.sh` installs `usr/bin/pdfcraft-cli` next to the app; the v0.4.0 x86_64 tarball is about 55 MB). Servers, CI and AI agent sandboxes only need the headless CLI and its opt-in MCP server. A CLI-only archive makes it a small, verifiable download.

### Nice to have
State the minimum glibc in the release notes (the Linux release builds on `ubuntu-22.04` runners, so glibc 2.35, as `release.yml` notes), or ship a static musl build.

Same request for PhotoCraft: storytold/photocraft#1616

title: Global units setting: default to millimetres from system locale
author: ch0kemeister
body:
## Summary

There is currently no way to make PdfCraft use metric units throughout. Millimetres can only be selected per dialog (and the choice is not remembered), while some places are hard-wired to inches. For users in metric countries this means switching units again and again.

## Current behaviour (main, a6bc63a)

- **Page boxes / crop dialog** (`crates/ui-egui/src/pageboxes.rs`): has an Inches / Millimetres / Points selector, but `BoxesDraft::default()` always starts with `Unit::Inches` and the selection is not persisted.
- **Measure tool** (`crates/ui-egui/src/measure_ui.rs`): the unit is a free text field defaulting to `"in"`.
- **Document properties → Advanced** (`crates/ui-egui/src/dialogs.rs`): page size is always formatted as `{:.2} × {:.2} in`, no way to see millimetres.
- **Settings**: no units option at all.

## Proposal

1. Add a global **Units** setting (Millimetres / Inches / Points, maybe Centimetres) in Settings, persisted in `app.ron`.
2. Default it from the system locale on first start: metric everywhere except en-US (and the few other inch countries), similar to what #158 asks for date fields.
3. Use that setting as the initial value in the page-boxes dialog and the measure tool, and for the page-size display in Document properties. Per-dialog overrides can stay.
4. Optional: remember the last unit chosen in a dialog.

Happy to test on macOS (Apple Silicon, German locale).

title: Windows: each UI test binary gets a 500–600 MB debug-symbol file, so one `cargo test --workspace` needs ~38 GB
author: pauliusiv123-rgb
body:
## What happens

On Windows, `target\debug\deps` reached 301 GB after three days of contributing: pulling `main` and running the gates from `CLAUDE.md`. Most of it is `.pdb` debug-symbol files:

| File type | Count | Size |
|---|---|---|
| `.pdb` | 777 | 258.3 GB |
| `.exe` | 676 | 29.5 GB |
| `.rlib` / `.rmeta` | 2,883 | 13.2 GB |

One complete debug build (the newest copy of each artifact) is about **38.5 GB, 31.4 GB of it PDBs**. So a contributor on Windows needs roughly 40 GB free to run `cargo test --workspace`, and more as old copies pile up. With less, the build fails partway through.

## Why

1. **Every integration-test file is its own binary.** There are 41 files in `crates/ui-egui/tests` (57 in the workspace). Each links the whole app (egui, wgpu, the renderer, the JS engine…), and on Windows each gets its own 500–600 MB PDB.
2. **Full debug info, dependencies included.** `[profile.dev.package."*"]` only sets `opt-level = 2`, so every dependency keeps full debug info too.
3. **Cargo never removes old artifacts.** When `Cargo.lock` changes (most pulls of `main`) or a different feature set is built (one package with `-p` instead of the workspace), new copies are built under new hashes next to the old ones. For example, `editing-*.exe` exists in 12 versions from the last three days, about 6.5 GB with their PDBs.

## Possible fixes

- **Less debug info for dependencies:** `debug = false` or `debug = "line-tables-only"` under `[profile.dev.package."*"]`. Our own crates keep full debug info. Dependency frames in a backtrace keep or lose line numbers depending on the option chosen.
- **Or less for everything:** `[profile.dev] debug = "line-tables-only"`. Backtraces keep file and line; stepping through locals in a debugger is lost.
- **One integration-test binary for `pdfcraft-ui-egui`:** for example `tests/ui/main.rs` with the current files as modules (`autotests = false` and one `[[test]]`). That's one link instead of 41, so a much smaller `target` and a faster …

title: Localize displayed keyboard shortcuts (German Ctrl → Strg)
author: Streetblock
body:
During the German UI review on Windows, the toolbar search hint still displays `Ctrl+K`. With a German interface, the expected display is `Strg+K`. Switching the interface language currently does not localize the shortcut key names.

This was observed in the local build with the German catalog being prepared. The existing formatting paths also bypass localization for the other interface languages.

### Reproduction

1. Run the Windows desktop app with the German interface catalog and select Deutsch.
2. Inspect the search hint in the top toolbar: it displays `Ctrl+K`.
3. Check menu shortcuts, command-palette details and the keyboard-shortcuts dialog for the same unlocalized key names.

Expected: the displayed names follow the active interface language, for example `Strg+K` and `Strg+Umschalt+S` in German. The actual key bindings remain the same.

### Code findings

- The toolbar hint calls egui's default `Context::format_shortcut`, outside the translation catalog: [widgets.rs](https://github.com/storytold/pdfcraft/blob/a6bc63a497954af87c1cd5a2a1e72e928a11c039/crates/ui-egui/src/widgets.rs#L67).
- Registered menu shortcuts, palette details and the help dialog use `Shortcut::label(mac)`. Its non-macOS branch hardcodes `Ctrl` and `Shift`: [engine/commands.rs](https://github.com/storytold/pdfcraft/blob/a6bc63a497954af87c1cd5a2a1e72e928a11c039/crates/engine/src/commands.rs#L71). Call sites are in `ui-egui/src/commands.rs`, `palette.rs` and `dialogs.rs`.
- Some toolbar/tooltips use literal macOS shortcut strings and should be included in the display audit.
- The pinned egui 0.36.2 exposes `ModifierNames` and `KeyboardShortcut::format(&ModifierNames, is_mac)`, so a UI formatter can supply localized modifier names. Merely adding a `Ctrl` entry to a TSV catalog will not affect the current calls.

### Suggested scope / acceptance

- Introduce a shared, language-aware UI shortcut formatter and use it consistently in the toolbar, menus, command palette, keyboard-shortcuts dialog…

author: meotao
body:
**What happens**

With Interface language set to 简体中文, Chinese UI text renders as replacement boxes (□). The tools list shows `□出 PDF` (导出 PDF), `填写与□名` (填写与签名), `□□ PDF` (编辑 PDF / 压缩 PDF), `□□页面` (组织页面), `准□表□` (准备表单), `使用□□` (使用证书), and the welcome line shows `□迎使用 PdfCraft` (欢迎使用 PdfCraft).

`crates/ui-egui/src/i18n/zh-hans.tsv` is complete, so this is font coverage, not translation: every box is exactly a Simplified-only codepoint (导 U+5BFC, 签 U+7B7E, 编 U+7F16, 辑 U+8F91, 组 U+7EC4, 织 U+7EC7, 压 U+538B, 缩 U+7F29, 备 U+5907, 单 U+5355, 图 U+56FE, 证 U+8BC1, 书 U+4E66, 查 U+67E5, 欢 U+6B22, 认 U+8BA4), while characters that share a codepoint with Japanese (所有, 工具, 密文, 合并文件, 页面, 添加, 表) render fine.

**Why**

`.github/workflows/release.yml` pins the craft-fonts build input at `abb83316d96aa59c1cf64784289e378fe9fa5695`, whose `fonts/manifest.txt` lists only `Jpan,Latn` faces (Shippori Mincho, BIZ UDPGothic Regular/Bold, BIZ UDMincho) — no `Hans` entry. So `pdfcraft_fonts::ui_chinese_fonts()` (`crates/fonts/src/craft.rs`) returns empty, `ui_cjk_fonts()` falls back to Japanese faces only, and egui — which draws each character with the first face that has it — falls through to the replacement glyph for every Simplified-only character.

Verify:

```
git show abb83316d96aa59c1cf64784289e378fe9fa5695:fonts/manifest.txt   # Jpan only
git show 8dcdacd5153e64560d109541a47d806f26f048c0:fonts/manifest.txt   # adds Noto Sans CJK SC ... Hans,Latn
```

1. Bump the craft-fonts pin to `8dcdacd5153e64560d109541a47d806f26f048c0` or later, which adds `Noto Sans CJK SC` (`Hans,Latn`).

title: Fill & Sign text loses characters outside Western European (written as ?)
author: kisst
body:
Fill & Sign text (Text, Date, and anything else drawn as a typewriter FreeText annotation) is written with the standard Helvetica font and WinAnsi encoding (`crates/annot/src/appearance.rs`). Any character outside Western European Latin becomes `?` in the saved appearance stream.

**Repro:** Fill & Sign ▸ Text, type `Dvořák`, `Ελληνικά`, `日本語` or `Русский`, save, and open the file in any viewer. The page shows `Dvo?ák`, `????????`, `???`, `???????`.

This affects every interface language whose script isn't Western European (cs, ja, zh-Hans, zh-Hant, ru, te). #505 adds a date format with localized month names. Until this is fixed, it refuses dates the PDF can't hold rather than saving `?`, but typed text still loses those characters.

**Probably needed:** draw these appearances with an embedded font subset (Type 0 / CIDFontType2 with ToUnicode), using the bundled UI fonts and craft-fonts when they're present. Fall back to Helvetica/WinAnsi only when every character fits, and refuse rather than write `?` otherwise.

title: OCR: accented Latin letters (German ä ö ü ß, French é è ç …) come out as „?“
author: martinjohuber
body:
With the OCR models installed (`cargo xtask models`), recognising a scanned German page turns every accented letter into „?“. The rest of the text is recognised well. Missing models in the release builds are a separate problem, tracked in #103 and #489.

**Steps** (PdfCraft built from `main` at 79eadc2, Windows 11)

1. Render a German text page at 200 dpi and make an image-only PDF from it (`doc_create` with `from: images`).
2. Run `ocr_recognize` with language `en`, the only one available.
3. `text_extract`:

```
Seite 1: Angebot
Sehr geehrte Damen und Herren,
vielen Dank f?r lhre Anfrage. Gerne ?bersenden wir Ihnen unser Angebot
f?r den Gro?format-Drucker mit F?rderband (Bauraum 2600 mm).
...
Mit freundlichen Gr??en
```

Expected: „für“, „übersenden“, „Großformat“, „Förderband“, „Grüßen“. The page has 14 umlauts and ß, and all 14 are lost. Searching the OCR'd PDF for „Förderband“ or „Größe“ finds nothing.

**Cause:** This is documented in `crates/ocr/src/lib.rs`: the ocrs models read the Latin alphabet without accents. It affects German, French, Spanish, Portuguese, Czech, Polish, the Nordic languages and others, so most European scans. The UI already speaks several of these languages.

**Possible directions:**
- The PP-OCR route from #433 also has a Latin recognition model covering accented European letters (Apache-2.0, same RTen/ONNX pipeline and `cargo xtask models` workflow). It could be added as a „Latin (accented)“ language next to `en`.
- Alternatively, an ocrs recognition model trained with an extended Latin alphabet.
- Until then, the OCR dialog could say that accented letters aren't recognised yet.

I can test candidate models on German, French and Spanish samples if that helps.

title: Document content stays US English in a translated UI: page-number tokens, date tokens, stamps, phone-number pattern
author: martinjohuber
body:
With the UI in German (or another translated language), what PdfCraft writes *into the document* is still US English or uses US formats. Fill & Sign dates are covered by #505/#158. These are the other places:

1. **Header & footer page-number tokens** (`crates/edit/src/lib.rs:204-207`)
   - `<<1 of n>>` → „2 of 5“, `<<Page 1>>` → „Page 2“, `<<Page 1 of n>>` → „Page 2 of 5“. The words are hard-coded.
   - The Header & Footer dialog offers exactly these five formats (`ui-egui/src/marks_ui.rs:111`), so a German user gets „Page 2 of 5“ in a German document.
   - Suggestion: localized tokens, e.g. `<<1 von n>>`, `<<Seite 1>>`, `<<Seite 1 von n>>`, offered in the dialog according to the interface language. Or let `of`/`Page` follow the interface language when the mark is created.

2. **Date tokens:** There is no dotted day-first format (`d.m.yyyy`, `dd.mm.yyyy`), which is the standard in German, Austrian, Swiss, Russian, Czech and Polish documents. `<<mmmm d, yyyy>>` only knows English month names. Something like `<<d. mmmm yyyy>>` with month names in the interface language would cover the common German form „9. Oktober 2026“. #505's date-code engine might be reusable here.

3. **Standard stamps:** „APPROVED“, „CONFIDENTIAL“, „DRAFT“ … are drawn in English whatever the interface language. Localized stamp sets, or at least the stamp text following the interface language, would let a German office use them.

4. **Redaction pattern „Phone Numbers“** (`crates/redact/src/patterns.rs`, `fn phone`)
   - It accepts only 10 digits, or 11 with a country code, i.e. the North American format.
   - For „+49 2151 123456“ (12 digits) it marks only „2151 123456“ and leaves „+49“ visible.
   - Most international numbers are missed or redacted partly, and a partly redacted number in a document the user thinks is clean is the worst case.
   - Suggestion: accept E.164 numbers with a leading `+` country code (up to 15 digits, grouped by spaces, dashes, dots or parentheses), and national numbe…

title: Feature Request: Shift+Click Text Selection and Cross-Page Text Selection
author: mapafe-notbot
body:
This might not be particularly important to many users, but there are two text selection features in Adobe Acrobat that are essential to my workflows and that I haven't been able to find in PDFCraft:

1. **Shift+Click text selection**: Select a word or some text, then hold Shift and click somewhere else in the document to extend the selection to include all the text in between.
2. **Cross-page text selection**: Select text by clicking and dragging the mouse across page boundaries, allowing continuous text selection over multiple pages.
Both features are very useful when working with longer PDF documents, and I would really appreciate seeing them implemented in PDFCraft.

title: [Bug]: Intermittent black screen on startup when launched via .desktop entry on Ubuntu
author: nbourre
body:
### Environment
- **OS:** Ubuntu (Linux x86_64)
- **Session Type:** Wayland
- **Graphics / Driver:** Mesa Intel(R) Iris(R) Xe Graphics (TGL GT2) / OpenGL vendor: Intel
- **App Version:** pdfcraft v0.4.0 / photocraft v0.5.0 (AppImage versions)
- **UI Framework:** egui / wgpu / winit

### Describe the Bug
When launching `pdfcraft` or `photocraft` AppImages by clicking the file in the GNOME file manager or via a configured `.desktop` launcher file, the application window framework opens but the interface canvas randomly gets stuck rendering a solid black screen. 

Crucially, launching the exact same AppImage binaries directly inside a terminal emulator (`Ctrl + Alt + T`) works flawlessly 100% of the time.

### Steps to Reproduce
1. Create a `.desktop` file pointing to the AppImage.
2. Launch the application from the desktop environment applications menu or dock.
3. The initial window frames load, but the interior graphics surface intermittently gets trapped in a black canvas state.

### Additional Context
Since this occurs on an Intel Iris Xe system running Wayland, it strongly points to an initialization race condition or surface format mismatch inside the `wgpu`/`winit` pipeline when spawned without an active TTY/shell environment context. 

Passing graphical fallback arguments like `--disable-gpu` did not fully resolve the intermittent failure.

### Workaround Update
I was able to completely resolve the intermittent black screen issue by explicitly setting the backend environment variable in the `.desktop` launcher. Forcing the application to use Vulkan fixes the problem:

Exec=env WGPU_BACKEND=vulkan /home/USERNAME/apps/pdfcraft-0.4.0-linux-x86_64.AppImage %U

title: Linux: publish a signed dnf repository so `dnf upgrade` updates PdfCraft
author: medukn
body:
## Problem

Each release attaches `.rpm` packages, but no package repository points at them. A user who
installs `pdfcraft-<ver>-linux-x86_64.rpm` with `dnf install` never hears about a new version:
`dnf upgrade`, GNOME Software and KDE Discover only see packages from configured repositories.
Updating means finding the release page, downloading the new `.rpm` and installing it by hand, for
every release.

The Linux RPMs are also unsigned. The release workflow has signing steps only for macOS and Windows
(and only when their secrets are configured). The RPM itself carries no publisher signature, and
dnf doesn't check signatures on local files by default (`localpkg_gpgcheck`). HTTPS and
`SHA256SUMS.txt` catch a corrupted download, but the checksum file isn't signed either.

The AppImage already updates itself through `.zsync`. The RPM, for Fedora, RHEL and openSUSE users,
has no update path. (The `.deb` has the same gap; see "Out of scope".)

## Proposal

Publish a signed RPM repository that follows the GitHub releases. On Fedora 41+ (dnf5; the
`config-manager` command comes from `dnf5-plugins`), users add it once:

```sh
sudo dnf config-manager addrepo --from-repofile=https://<host>/rpm/pdfcraft.repo
sudo dnf install pdfcraft
# from then on, `sudo dnf upgrade` (or GNOME Software) picks up new releases
```

with a repo file like:

```ini
[pdfcraft]
name=PdfCraft
baseurl=https://<host>/rpm/stable/$basearch
enabled=1
gpgcheck=1
repo_gpgcheck=1
gpgkey=https://<host>/rpm/pdfcraft-archive-key.asc
```

dnf asks the user to trust the key on first use, and may ask twice, because it keeps keys for
metadata and packages separately. The docs should give the fingerprint to compare against each
time. Instructions for other distributions (RHEL/EPEL, openSUSE via `zypper addrepo`) can follow
once each has been tested.

## Suggested implementation

This fits the current release flow (`docs/releasing.md`): CI builds a **draft**, and a maintainer
publishes it in the GitHub UI.

title: Linux (GNOME Wayland): window title bar doesn't match the desktop theme
author: fqazzazee
body:
## Environment

- Fedora 44, GNOME Shell 50.5, Wayland session, 167% display scaling
- Built from source at `653f826`

## Title bar doesn't follow the GNOME theme (Wayland)

On GNOME Wayland, the app draws its own title bar. This app shows winit's plain fallback bar, which
ignores the GNOME theme, dark mode and button layout.

The workspace sets `eframe = { version = "0.36", default-features = false }` (`Cargo.toml:67`),
which also drops winit's default `wayland-csd-adwaita` feature, so `sctk-adwaita` isn't in
`Cargo.lock`.

Possible fixes:

- Enable `winit/wayland-csd-adwaita`, so the title bar follows GNOME's look and light/dark mode, or
- Draw an in-app title bar, as PhotoCraft does on Linux.

Workaround: start the app through Xwayland (`env -u WAYLAND_DISPLAY pdfcraft`), so GNOME draws a real
title bar.

Same issue in GridCraft, with more detail: https://github.com/storytold/gridcraft/issues/54

title: Windows: Outlook PDF attachment launch crashes when restored HiDPI window exceeds 8192px
author: msaulc
body:
PdfCraft 0.4.0 on Windows crashes immediately when opening a PDF attachment directly from classic Outlook. Saving the same attachment to Downloads and double-clicking it succeeds. The Windows `.pdf` association correctly invokes `pdfcraft.exe "%1"`.

The failure occurs before document rendering:

```text
wgpu error: Validation Error
Caused by:
  In Surface::configure
    `Surface` width and height must be within the maximum supported texture size.
    Requested was (8600, 3423), maximum extent for either dimension is 8192.
```

The saved `window` settings included:

```text
fullscreen:false,maximized:true,inner_size_points:Some((x:3440.0,y:1369.0))
```

This machine uses several monitors with different sizes/scales and Intel Arc / NVIDIA RTX 4070 Laptop graphics. The requested dimensions correspond to the saved point dimensions multiplied by 2.5; the precise reason the Outlook launch chooses that initial scale has not yet been established.

Reproduction on the affected installation:

2. Open a PDF attachment directly from classic Outlook.
3. PdfCraft logs the surface validation error and exits. Keeping another PdfCraft instance open does not avoid the crash.
4. Save that same PDF to Downloads and open it there: it works.

author: taylorandrew07-lab
body:
## Summary
Combine files is a table today: files, page ranges, sort and drag. I'd like to add a **grid view**, where each file is a thumbnail of its first page. Each file can then be **expanded into its pages**, so pages can be reordered or removed before combining. This is how Combine works in Acrobat, and it's the main thing I miss when merging scanned reports and photo sets.

I plan to implement this myself, in small PRs. I'm opening this first so you can steer the design before any code lands.

## Proposed PRs
1. **Grid view and zoom**

title: Discuss a pure-Rust RSA signing backend and the scope of the Marvin advisory
author: Streetblock
body:
PdfCraft's native RSA signing backend uses `aws-lc-rs`, which brings AWS-LC's C/assembly implementation into the product build. `CLAUDE.md` still states “Rust only in the product and build”. This issue is to discuss the intended dependency policy and an evidence-based route back to a pure-Rust signing backend.

### Current implementation

AWS-LC was introduced with the initial signing crate in [e06a98a](https://github.com/storytold/pdfcraft/commit/e06a98adaa22595b41801c0ab1888680c8201566), on 2026-10-02. The README and `deny.toml` cite RUSTSEC-2023-0071 / ADR-0009: RustCrypto RSA is used for public-key verification, while native private-key import, generation and signing use AWS-LC.

At [90bb2f1](https://github.com/storytold/pdfcraft/blob/90bb2f14ad4c60f84d900c1389e289e51a5ce7a6/crates/sign/src/keys.rs), AWS-LC is largely contained in `keys.rs`. Software RSA signs with RSASSA-PKCS1-v1.5 and SHA-256/384/512. This crate does not provide an RSA decryption/unpadding path; PKCS#12 password encryption uses symmetric RustCrypto primitives. ECDSA P-256/P-384 already use RustCrypto, and browser RSA signing/key generation are refused.

### The security distinction

The [original Marvin description](https://people.redhat.com/~hkario/marvin/) requires an attacker-accessible RSA **decryption** timing oracle. Such an oracle can also be used to forge signatures, including when the same key is exposed through another service. A signing-only API does not itself provide that oracle.

This does **not** establish that RustCrypto's signing implementation is free of other timing side channels. [RUSTSEC-2023-0071](https://rustsec.org/advisories/RUSTSEC-2023-0071.html) still lists no patched versions, and [rsa 0.10.0-rc.19](https://github.com/RustCrypto/RSA/blob/v0.10.0-rc.19/README.md), released on 2026-10-06, still carries the warning. PdfCraft currently pins rc.18.

RustCrypto is actively tracking private-operation hardening in [#711](https://github.com/RustCrypto/RSA/issues/711). Exist…

## Description

Please add a workflow for importing SVG files, placing them on PDF pages, manipulating them, and saving the resulting document while preserving vector quality.

The reference workflow is Open PDF Studio: I tested importing custom SVG symbols directly into the application. This made it possible to use a small electrical symbol library without building the application or preparing a complex collection package.

I would like a similarly accessible workflow in PDFCraft, implemented independently using its own architecture.

Allow users to annotate and compose technical drawings with their own reusable vector symbols.

**Import SVG → preview → place on a PDF page → move/resize/rotate → duplicate as needed → save PDF → reopen with the symbols intact.**

title: `pdfcraft-cli mcp` silently accepts unknown options, so a mistyped `--root` runs unconfined
author: sawizzle
body:
## Summary
`pdfcraft-cli mcp --totally-bogus-flag` starts normally with exit 0 and serves every tool. #133 fixed the same class of problem for `edit`, but `mcp` still has it.

## Why it matters
`--root` is the sandbox. A typo such as `--rot DIR` or `--root=DIR` (if that form isn't parsed) starts a server that can read and write anywhere, and nothing tells you. In my test, `--root <dir>` correctly blocked `C:/Windows/...`; with an unknown flag instead, the same server opened files outside that dir.

It also hides version skew. `docs/mcp.md` documents `--compact`, but the v0.4.0 release binary accepts it without complaint and still lists all 131 tools.

## Repro (Windows 11, pdfcraft-cli 0.4.0 MSI)
1. `pdfcraft-cli mcp --totally-bogus-flag`: initialises, and `doc_open` on any path succeeds
2. `pdfcraft-cli mcp --compact`: `tools/list` returns 131 tools

## Suggested fix
Reject unknown `mcp` options with exit 2 and a usage line, as `effectcraft-cli` does (`unknown option --totally-bogus`).

title: Forms: PDFs that list their fields only as page widgets show nothing fillable (empty /AcroForm /Fields)
author: edurbs
body:
## Summary
Opening a PDF whose AcroForm dictionary has an empty (or missing) `/Fields` array shows the form drawn on the page, but PdfCraft finds zero form fields: nothing is highlighted, the Fields panel is empty, and `form_fields`/`form_fill` see no fields. The same file fills fine in Acrobat, the browsers and MuPDF.

## Why it matters
These files are real: some producers write every field as a merged widget annotation in the page `/Annots` (`/FT`, `/T`, `/V`, `/AP`, no `/Parent`) and never list them in the `/Fields` tree. The file that prompted this (an ERP-generated AcroForm) has `NeedAppearances`, a 23-entry `/CO` calculation order and 533 text widgets across 2 pages. `pdfcraft-cli run` with `form_fields` returned `count: 0` on it, while MuPDF lists all 533 widgets as fillable — so the user's form is silently dead in PdfCraft.

`pdfcraft_forms::fields()` (`crates/forms/src/lib.rs`) enumerates only the `/Fields` tree, and the renderer's inspector (`crates/render/src/inspect.rs`) has its own `/Fields`-only walk, so the Fields panel count and the "N interactive form fields" notice miss them too. The `/CO` scripts bind to fields by object reference through the same enumeration, so calculations can't run either.

## Repro
A minimal file shows it (also the shape of the real one):

```
1 0 obj << /Type /Catalog /Pages 2 0 R /AcroForm 4 0 R >> endobj
2 0 obj << /Type /Pages /Kids [3 0 R] /Count 1 >> endobj
3 0 obj << /Type /Page /Parent 2 0 R /MediaBox [0 0 200 200] /Annots [5 0 R 6 0 R] >> endobj
4 0 obj << /Fields [] >> endobj
5 0 obj << /Type /Annot /Subtype /Widget /FT /Tx /T (alpha) /Rect [10 100 90 120] >> endobj
6 0 obj << /Type /Annot /Subtype /Widget /FT /Tx /T (beta) /Rect [10 60 90 80] >> endobj
trailer << /Root 1 0 R >>
%%EOF
```

`pdfcraft-cli run --script` with `doc_open` + `form_fields` on it returns `count: 0`.

## Suggested fix
Adopt widget annotations that no `/Fields` entry reaches as fields, as Acrobat and the browsers do — through each widget's top…

title: Linux: the Print dialog lists only "Save as PDF" when the printers are driverless IPP destinations no local queue exists for
author: edurbs
body:
**Symptom** (Ubuntu, .deb install; same family as #644 and #465, which are Windows):

File ▸ Print lists only **Save as PDF** — none of the system's printers — although the same printers appear and print from GTK/Qt applications (Firefox, LibreOffice, Evince…).

**Root cause**

The dialog's printer list is `lpstat -p -d` (`crates/print/src/spool.rs`). `-p` lists only **permanent CUPS queues**. A driverless IPP printer discovered on the network — the standard way printing works on modern Linux desktops — has no permanent queue: GTK lists it through libcups `cupsEnumDests`, and CUPS builds a **temporary queue** only when a job is actually sent. `cups-browsed` usually materializes permanent queues for such printers, but it can be disabled, not installed, or lose the race — and until it does, `lpstat -p` shows nothing while every GTK dialog shows the printer.

Only `lpstat -e` (CUPS ≥ 1.7, 2013) lists these queue-less destinations. Printing to them already works from PdfCraft's code path: `lp -d NAME` makes CUPS create the temporary queue and accept the job.

**Reproduction** (Debian forky / CUPS 2.4.18, no real printer needed)

```console
$ sudo apt install cups-ipp-utils
$ /usr/sbin/ippeveprinter MyPrinter        # advertises a driverless IPP printer via DNS-SD

$ lpstat -p -d                              # what PdfCraft reads
no system default destination               # MyPrinter is invisible here
$ lpstat -e
MyPrinter                                   # listed here

$ pdfcraft-cli run printers
{ "count": 0, "printers": [] }              # dialog shows only "Save as PDF"

$ lp -d MyPrinter -t test doc.pdf           # yet printing to it works
request id is MyPrinter-1 (1 file(s))
```

**Two aggravating factors**

- The `.deb`/`.rpm` packages recommend no `cups-client`, so on a machine without a print stack `lpstat` is missing entirely and the list is empty with no hint why.
- Enumeration failures are silent: a missing `lpstat`, a stopped scheduler (`lpstat: Scheduler…
