title: doc_create: TIFF decode is capped at 256 MiB while PNG is not — "decoder limits exceeded" on print-sized images
author: r-neuschulz
body:
## Problem

Importing a large image with `doc_create {"from":"images"}` fails with `decoder limits exceeded` once the **decoded** TIFF exceeds **256 MiB**, while PNG of the same and larger decoded size imports fine. For print work this bites at ordinary poster sizes: a 12000x16000 CMYK TIFF (the exact pixel count for a 960x1280 mm page at 317.5 ppi) is 768 MB decoded and cannot be imported at all.

The cap appears to be byte-based on the decoded buffer and applied only on the TIFF path. There is no flag or environment variable to raise it — the binary only carries `PDFCRAFT_MODELS` and `PDFCRAFT_TEXT_DEBUG`.

## Repro

`pdfcraft-cli 0.4.0`, official Windows x64 MSI. The test images are solid white, so they compress to well under 1 MB each while still decoding to hundreds of MB — handy as repro files:

```sh
# 12000x16000 CMYK TIFF -> 1.0 MB file, 768 MB decoded
photocraft-cli run --new '{"width":12000,"height":16000}' \
  --cmd image.mode.cmyk --out big_cmyk.tif --format tif

# same pixels as PNG, RGB -> 0.6 MB file, 576 MB decoded
photocraft-cli run --new '{"width":12000,"height":16000}' --out big_rgb.png --format png
```

Then, over the MCP server (`pdfcraft-cli mcp`):

```json
{"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"doc_create",
 "arguments":{"from":"images","paths":["big_cmyk.tif"]}}}
```

| file | px | ch | decoded bytes | vs 256 MiB | result |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| TIFF CMYK | 12000x4000 | 4 | 192,000,000 | under | ok |
| TIFF CMYK | 12000x5000 | 4 | 240,000,000 | under | ok |
| TIFF RGB | 12000x7400 | 3 | 266,400,000 | under | ok |
| TIFF RGB | 12000x7500 | 3 | 270,000,000 | **over** | `decoder limits exceeded` |
| TIFF CMYK | 12000x6000 | 4 | 288,000,000 | over | `decoder limits exceeded` |

title: doc_create drops the embedded ICC profile: a CMYK JPEG becomes /DeviceCMYK with no /ICCBased
author: r-neuschulz
body:
## Problem

`doc_create {"from":"images"}` discards the embedded ICC profile. A CMYK JPEG carrying a 236 KB output profile becomes a `/DeviceCMYK` image XObject with no `/ICCBased` wrapper anywhere in the file, so the PDF holds CMYK numbers with nothing stating which CMYK space they are in. A RIP or preflight has to guess, and the same file will separate differently depending on who opens it.

The image data itself is carried over perfectly — `/DCTDecode`, `/Length` byte-identical to the source JPEG, 12000x16000 — it is only the colour space that is downgraded from ICC-tagged to device-dependent.

## Repro

`pdfcraft-cli 0.4.0`, official Windows x64 MSI. A 64x64 image is enough.

```sh
photocraft-cli run --new '{"width":64,"height":64}' \
  --cmd image.mode.cmyk --params '{"profile":"coated-cmyk"}' \
  --out cmyk.jpg --format jpg
```

The input JPEG carries the profile and the Adobe marker:

```
APP14 Adobe marker present
SOF: 64x64, 4 components
embedded ICC = 236836 bytes   (four APP2 ICC_PROFILE chunks)
```

Import it and save:

```json
{"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"doc_create",
 "arguments":{"from":"images","paths":["cmyk.jpg"]}}}
{"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"doc_save",
 "arguments":{"doc":1,"path":"out.pdf","full":true}}}
```

Inspecting `out.pdf` (searching the raw bytes and every inflated object stream):

| | input JPEG | output PDF |
|---|---|---|
| colour space | CMYK, ICC-tagged | `/DeviceCMYK` |
| ICC profile | 236,836 bytes | **absent**, no `/ICCBased` |
| image data | `/DCTDecode` | `/DCTDecode`, same bytes |

Same result on a 12000x16000 CMYK JPEG: `/DeviceCMYK`, no `/ICCBased`, image stream byte-identical.

## Suggested behaviour

Wrap the image in an `/ICCBased` colour space built from the profile in the source file, with `/N` 4 for CMYK, 3 for RGB and 1 for Gray, falling back to the current `/Device*` behaviour only when the source has no profile. Photoshop and Acrobat both preserve the tag on import, and for CMYK it is the di…

title: pdfa_convert always writes an sRGB output intent, even for CMYK-only documents, and pdfa_verify calls it compliant
author: r-neuschulz
body:
## Problem

`pdfa_convert` always embeds an **sRGB** output intent, even when the document contains no RGB at all. On a CMYK-only document it writes `sRGB IEC61966-2.1` as the output condition, and `pdfa_verify` then reports `"compliant": true` with `"issues": []`.

The file passes PDF/A-2b because an output intent is present, but the output intent describes a colour space the document does not use. The intended output condition is the one piece of colour information a RIP relies on, so a CMYK file that announces sRGB is worse than one that announces nothing — and the verifier gives no hint that anything is off.

## Repro

`pdfcraft-cli 0.4.0`, official Windows x64 MSI. 64x64 is enough.

```sh
photocraft-cli run --new '{"width":64,"height":64}' \
  --cmd image.mode.cmyk --params '{"profile":"coated-cmyk"}' \
  --out cmyk.jpg --format jpg
```

```json
{"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"doc_create",
 "arguments":{"from":"images","paths":["cmyk.jpg"]}}}
{"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"pdfa_convert","arguments":{"doc":1,"level":"2b"}}}
```

Result:

```json
{"compliant": true,
 "declared": {"output_intents": ["sRGB IEC61966-2.1"], "pdfa": "PDF/A-2b", "pdfua": null},
 "issues": [],
 "level": "PDF/A-2b"}
```

The saved file then contains, in the catalog, an output intent of `sRGB IEC61966-2.1` with `/S /GTS_PDFA1`, while the only image on the page is `/DeviceCMYK`. `pdfa_verify {"doc":1,"level":"2b"}` returns the same `"compliant": true, "issues": []`.

Confirmed identically on a real 12000x16000 CMYK page at 960x1280 mm and at 1155x1540 mm.

## Suggested behaviour

- Choose the output intent from the document's actual colour usage: a CMYK output profile when the page content is CMYK, sRGB when it is RGB. Where the source image carried an ICC profile, that profile is the natural candidate (it is currently dropped on import — see #666).
- Let the caller supply one, e.g. `pdfa_convert {"doc":1,"level":"2b","output_intent":"/path/to/FOGRA39.icc"}`. Prepress us…

title: Build failure on Windows 11: non-exhaustive patterns error in pdfcraft-sign (windows.rs)
author: gitcloud
body:
### Environment
* **OS:** Windows 11
* **Toolchain:** Rust (cargo)
* **Commit version:** Latest master branch

### Problem Description
When attempting to compile `pdfcraft` natively on Windows 11 using `cargo run --release -p pdfcraft`, the compilation process fails during the `pdfcraft-sign` crate phase. 

The compiler throws a compilation error `E0004` regarding non-exhaustive patterns because recent additions to the `PublicKey` enum (such as `P521`, `Brainpool`, and `Ed25519`) have not been mapped or handled inside the Windows-specific platform implementation file (`crates\sign\src\windows.rs`).

### Terminal Error Output
```cmd
   Compiling pdfcraft-sign v0.4.0 (C:\Users\mikec\Documents\GitHub\pdfcraft\crates\sign)
error[E0004]: non-exhaustive patterns: `&keys::PublicKey::P521(_)`, `&keys::PublicKey::BrainpoolP256(_)`, `&keys::PublicKey::BrainpoolP384(_)` and 3 more not covered
   --> crates\sign\src\windows.rs:26:15
    |
 26 |         match &self.public {
    |               ^^^^^^^^^^^^ patterns `&keys::PublicKey::P521(_)`, `&keys::PublicKey::BrainpoolP256(_)`, `&keys::PublicKey::BrainpoolP384(_)` and 3 more not covered

error[E0004]: non-exhaustive patterns: `&keys::PublicKey::P521(_)`, `&keys::PublicKey::BrainpoolP256(_)`, `&keys::PublicKey::BrainpoolP384(_)` and 3 more not covered
   --> crates\sign\src\windows.rs:66:31
    |
 66 |         let supported = match &certificate.public_key {
    |                               ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^

error: could not compile `pdfcraft-sign` (lib) due to 2 previous errors
```

### Suggested Resolution
Add a wildcard baseline fallback match arm (`_ => ...`) to the match statements on lines 26 and 66 within `crates\sign\src\windows.rs` to satisfy strict type-checking on Windows platforms when new key variants are introduced.

title: v0.4.0 ships without the Hans UI face — Simplified Chinese UI shows replacement glyphs
author: hswqg
body:
**Title:**

v0.4.0 ships without the Hans UI face — Simplified Chinese UI shows replacement glyphs

**Labels（如可选）:** `bug`, `fonts`, `i18n`

**Body:**

## Environment

- PdfCraft **v0.4.0**, Windows x64 MSI (`pdfcraft-0.4.0-windows-x64.msi`, sha256 `76e61e27…43e3a`)
- UI language: 简体中文 (zh-hans)

## Symptom

With the UI language set to Simplified Chinese, characters that exist only in the Simplified script render as the replacement glyph (tofu), while characters shared with Japanese render fine. Affected UI words include: 页面 设置 视图 删除 缩放 旋转 书签 编辑 (页 设 视 图 删 缩 转 书 签 编 辑 …). Words like 文件 保存 打开 搜索 打印 display normally — they fall through to the embedded Japanese face (BIZ UDPGothic), which lacks the Simplified-only code points.

## Root cause

`.github/workflows/release.yml` pins the craft-fonts build input to `abb83316d96aa59c1cf64784289e378fe9fa5695` ("Bump deliberately"). That ref **predates** craft-fonts commit `8dcdacd` ("Fonts: Noto Sans CJK SC and Noto Sans Arabic"), so the v0.4.0 release binaries embed the `Jpan` faces but no `Hans` (and no `Arab`) face.

This is the exact failure mode documented in `crates/fonts/README.md`:

> `ui_chinese_fonts`: the `Hans` faces for the interface, in manifest order (without one, Chinese characters the Japanese faces lack show the replacement glyph).

## Evidence

I extracted the font assets embedded in the shipped `pdfcraft.exe` (v0.4.0, x64). It contains 13 faces: Ubuntu-Light, Hack, Noto Emoji, the egui icon font, Inter Regular/Medium/SemiBold, JetBrains Mono, Dancing Script, BIZ UDPGothic Regular/Bold, BIZ UDMincho, Shippori Mincho — **no Noto Sans CJK SC (`NotoSansCJKsc-Regular.otf`) and no Noto Sans Arabic**.

Checking BIZ UDPGothic's cmap against the zh-hans catalog confirms the missing code points, e.g.:

| Char | Code point | In BIZ UDPGothic? |
|---|---|---|
| 页 | U+9875 | ✗ |
| 设 | U+8BBE | ✗ |
| 视 | U+89C6 | ✗ |
| 删 | U+5220 | ✗ |
| 缩 | U+7F29 | ✗ |
| 转 | U+8F6C | ✗ |
| 书/签 | U+4E66/U+7B7E | ✗ |
| 编/辑 | U+7F16/U+8F9…

title: Update check shows a bare "http status: 403" when GitHub rate-limits anonymous requests
author: Shaun-Codes
body:
## Environment

- PdfCraft 0.4.0 (macOS DMG), macOS 27.0 arm64
- Network fine; `github.com` reachable in a browser

## Steps

1. Help ▸ Check for updates… (or ⌘K → `updates`)
2. Dialog shows: "Couldn't check for updates: couldn't reach GitHub (http status: 403)"

## What is actually happening

Replaying the app's request shows GitHub refusing with `403 API rate limit exceeded`
(`x-ratelimit-limit: 60`, `x-ratelimit-remaining: 0`). The check asks anonymously,
so it shares GitHub's 60-requests-per-hour bucket with every client behind the same
public IP (home NAT, office, VPN, carrier-grade NAT). The quota resets hourly; the
app is fine and the network is fine.

## Expected

When GitHub answers 403 with `X-RateLimit-Reset`, say what is wrong and when to
retry — e.g. "GitHub is rate-limiting update checks right now (shared hourly quota).
Try again in N minutes." — instead of a bare `http status: 403` that reads like the
app or the network is broken. The dialog already links the releases page, so users
can still update by hand in the meantime.

## Scope

Not asking to lift the limit (impossible without authentication) and not auto-update
(see #99): only that the failure message tells the truth. Happy to implement the
403 + `X-RateLimit-Reset` handling in `apps/pdfcraft/src/updates.rs` with a unit test.

author: MAX-2099
body: ## 问题描述 在 Windows 上切换到简体中文后，整个 UI 界面的中文字符全部显示为方框（豆腐块 / tofu）。 ## 复现步骤 1. Windows 系统 2. `cargo run --bin pdfcraft` 启动程序 3. 设置 → 语言 → 简体中文 4. 所有中文菜单、按钮文字变成 □□□ ## 根本原因 `crates/ui-egui/src/system_fonts.rs` 中的 `candidates()` 函数，Windows 下的备用字体列表只有西文字体： ```rust ["segoeui.ttf", "tahoma.ttf", "arial.ttf"] 这些字体都不包含中文字形。而且 `read()` 函数用阿拉伯字母 `\u{0627}` 作为 PROBE 检测字符，即使把 `msyh.ttc`（微软雅黑）加入列表，也会因为微软雅黑不包含阿拉伯字母而通不过检测，被跳过。 启动日志可以验证： pdfcraft_ui_egui::system_fonts: interface font fallback: C:\Windows\Fonts\segoeui.ttf ``` ## 修复方案 修改 `crates/ui-egui/src/system_fonts.rs` 两处： ### 修改 1：`candidates()` 中把微软雅黑加入 Windows 字体列表最前面 ``` // 改前 ["segoeui.ttf", "tahoma.ttf", "arial.ttf"].iter().map(|f| dir.join("Fonts").join(f)).collect() // 改后 ["msyh.ttc", "segoeui.ttf", "tahoma.ttf", "arial.ttf"].iter().map(|f| dir.join("Fonts").join(f)).collect() ``` ### 修改 2：`read()` 中对 `msyh.ttc` 跳过 PROBE 检测，直接使用第一个字体面 ``` // 改前 let index = face_with(&bytes, PROBE)?; // 改后 let index = if path.file_name().is_some_and(|n| n == "msyh.ttc") { 0 } else { face_with(&bytes, PROBE)? }; ``` ## 修复效果 修复后启动日志变为： ``` pdfcraft_ui_egui::system_fonts: interface font fallback: C:\Windows\Fonts\msyh.ttc ``` 简体中文界面正常显示，不再出现豆腐块。 ## 环境 - OS: Windows - GPU: AMD Radeon RX 6600 (DX12) - 版本: PdfCraft 0.5.0 #

title: Fixed zoom percentages draw pages at a different size from Acrobat (Page Display resolution)
author: cyfung1031
body:
## Summary

At the same fixed zoom percentage, PdfCraft draws a page at a different on-screen size from Adobe Acrobat.

PdfCraft fixes 100% to 96 dpi, which is `96 / 72` logical pixels per PDF point. Acrobat exposes a separate **Page Display ▸ Resolution** preference with two choices documented by Adobe:

- **Use System Setting** — use the system setting for monitor resolution.
- **Custom Resolution** — use a user-specified monitor resolution.

Acrobat's zoom percentage is a separate value. Adobe's JavaScript API treats zoom as a percentage (`100` = 100%, `200` = 200%, etc.).

So the useful model is not “choose a DPI for every zoom.” Acrobat has one display-resolution / monitor-PPI basis, and fixed zoom percentages scale relative to that basis. PdfCraft currently has no equivalent resolution preference and always uses a 96 dpi basis.

On the machine tested, Acrobat was set to Custom Resolution 110 ppi, and at the same percentage its pages were about 15% larger than PdfCraft's.

Adobe documentation:

- Page Display preferences, including **Use System Setting** and **Custom Resolution**: https://helpx.adobe.com/acrobat/using/viewing-pdfs-viewing-preferences.html
- Acrobat JavaScript `Doc.zoom`, where zoom is an independent percentage (`100` = 100%): https://opensource.adobe.com/dc-acrobat-sdk-docs/library/jsapiref/doc.html?highlight=selectpagenthword

## Expected behaviour

A page at a given fixed percentage should have the same intended on-screen size, in logical pixels per PDF point, as in Acrobat under equivalent display-resolution settings.

This does **not** imply a separate DPI choice for each zoom level. The resolution preference is the baseline; the zoom percentage scales that baseline.

Users who switch between Acrobat and PdfCraft should not notice a systematic fixed-percentage size difference when both are configured to the same resolution basis. Until that is implemented, the gap should be documented, and the parity manifest should say so.

Fit Width, Fit …

title: fix(automation): action_run reports success after replacing an earlier batch result

body:
## Summary

A batch containing different PDFs with the same basename produces one saved result even though `action_run` reports success for both inputs. The second processed PDF replaces the first processed PDF in the destination folder. This loses a generated result and requires the caller to run it again. The original input PDFs remained unchanged in the reproduction.

## Steps to reproduce

Use either build described under Runtime or environment. Save the following as `reproduce.py` in an empty disposable directory, put `pdfcraft-cli` on `PATH`, and run `python3 reproduce.py`. Alternatively pass the binary's absolute path as the first argument. The script generates its own PDFs without fonts or external assets, creates a fresh root, and keeps every input and output inside it. Each subprocess has a 60-second timeout. The exact script was executed with both tested builds.

from pathlib import Path
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile

assert binary, 'Put pdfcraft-cli on PATH or pass its absolute path.'

title: fix(automation): bookmark splitting reports success after replacing an earlier part
author: coygeek
body:
## Summary

Splitting a document at two top-level bookmarks with the same title produces two reported page ranges but only one output PDF. The later range replaces the earlier generated part in an initially empty output folder. The input PDF remains unchanged, so callers can recover the missing output by splitting again with explicit page boundaries.

## Steps to reproduce

Use either tested build listed under Runtime or environment, with pdfcraft-cli on PATH. Run this Python script in a fresh disposable directory. It creates a valid three-page PDF without fonts or external assets. Its page widths are 101, 102 and 103 points so reopening the output identifies which source pages survived.

```python
import hashlib
import json
import subprocess
from pathlib import Path

root = Path("work").resolve()
root.mkdir()
objects = [
    b"<< /Type /Catalog /Pages 2 0 R >>",
    b"<< /Type /Pages /Kids [3 0 R 4 0 R 5 0 R] /Count 3 >>",
]
for width in (101, 102, 103):
    objects.append(
        f"<< /Type /Page /Parent 2 0 R /MediaBox [0 0 {width} 100] /Resources << >> >>".encode()
    )
pdf = bytearray(b"%PDF-1.4\n")
offsets = [0]
for number, obj in enumerate(objects, 1):
    offsets.append(len(pdf))
    pdf.extend(f"{number} 0 obj\n".encode() + obj + b"\nendobj\n")

pdf.extend(
    f"trailer\n<< /Size {len(offsets)} /Root 1 0 R >>\nstartxref\n{xref}\n%%EOF\n".encode()
)
(root / "in.pdf").write_bytes(pdf)

title: fix(cli): edit reports success after truncating unsupported rotation degrees
author: coygeek
body:
## Summary

The one-shot page rotation command accepts a degree value that is not a multiple of 90, saves a different rotation, and exits successfully. Asking for 45 degrees writes an unrotated output; asking for 91 or 135 degrees writes a 90-degree rotation. The valid input PDF remains unchanged when the caller saves to a new path.

## Steps to reproduce

Put either tested executable from Runtime or environment on PATH as `pdfcraft-cli`. Run this in an empty disposable directory with Python 3. It creates a valid blank one-page PDF without fonts, images, or a preexisting document, then executes the unsupported-angle cases and valid controls. Each subprocess has a 30-second timeout and each output uses a new name.

```sh
python3 - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
import re
import subprocess

objects = [
    b'<< /Type /Catalog /Pages 2 0 R >>',
    b'<< /Type /Pages /Kids [3 0 R] /Count 1 /MediaBox [0 0 200 300] >>',

title: Fill & Sign: a placed signature can't be moved while a Fill & Sign tool is active
author: LloydNicholson
body:
## What happens
After placing a signature with Fill & Sign, it can't be dragged to a new position while any Fill & Sign tool is active (Sign, Initials, Add text, Check, Date):
- dragging the signature does nothing; it stays where it is;
- hovering over it shows a crosshair instead of the Move cursor;
- clicking it stamps another mark on top (or opens a text box with Add text).

So it looks as if signatures can't be moved once they're placed.

## Steps to reproduce
1. Open any PDF and choose **Fill & Sign › Sign**. Type a name and click **Apply**.
2. Click on the page to place the signature.
3. Choose another Fill & Sign tool, for example **Check**.
4. Drag the placed signature.

**Expected:** the signature moves, as it does in Acrobat, where placed Fill & Sign items can be picked up without changing tools.
**Actual:** nothing moves. Clicking the signature adds a check mark on top of it.

Reproduced on PdfCraft 0.5.0 (macOS, Apple silicon).

## Workaround
Press **V** (or click the arrow) to switch to the **Select** tool, then drag the signature or its handles. Right after a signature is placed, PdfCraft switches to Select by itself, so moving it straight away works. It only gets stuck once another Fill & Sign tool is chosen.

## Fix

title: Proposal: stet-pdf-reader as the renderer in place of hayro, now or as the bridge to M2
author: AndyCappDev
body:
I'm the author of [stet](https://github.com/AndyCappDev/stet), a PostScript and PDF
renderer in pure Rust (MIT OR Apache-2.0). I emailed Brandon about this yesterday; I'm
posting it here as well so that anyone working on M2 can weigh in.

The ROADMAP calls hayro "the bootstrap renderer" and makes M2 (your own model crate, font
engine and DisplayList devices, 150–250 h) the first priority. I'd like to suggest
[`stet-pdf-reader`](https://crates.io/crates/stet-pdf-reader) as a replacement for hayro,
either for good or as a better bootstrap until M2 is done.

### Why it might fit

- **It is already a display-list design.** A page is interpreted once into a
  `DisplayList`, a documented intermediate form
  ([docs/DISPLAY-LIST.md](https://github.com/AndyCappDev/stet/blob/main/docs/DISPLAY-LIST.md))
  whose enums are `#[non_exhaustive]` so that third-party renderers can be written
  against it. The rasteriser, the PDF writer and text extraction are all consumers of
  that list. This is the architecture ADR-0004 describes, and it exists today.
- **Tiles do not re-interpret the page.** #623 notes that every 1024 px tile
  re-interprets the whole page. With a display list, the page is interpreted once and
  any region is rendered from the list, with a per-render layer set. On the A1 sheet
  from #623, stet 0.8.5 draws the complete page (title block, revision table, Japanese
  labels) at 300 dpi in 11 s on my machine, with no content limit to raise. The cost is
  memory; see the caveats.
- **It is built for print and prepress.** DeviceCMYK, ICCBased, Separation and DeviceN
  are carried through the display list rather than flattened to RGB on the way in.
  Overprint and overprint mode are simulated, output intents are honoured, and black
  point compensation and per-object rendering intents are applied. Most of the Ghent
  Workgroup conformance files and PDF/X-4 samples render correctly, where pdf.js,
  poppler and pdfium show wrong colours. It is not yet at Acrobat parity on …

title: Combine Files keeps every copy of an image when its /ColorSpace is an indirect name (ImageMagick PDFs)
author: mlkonrad
body:
Combine Files is meant to store identical images once (`organize::combine_selected` runs `dedupe::dedupe_resources`), but images in PDFs written by ImageMagick are never merged. Every copy is kept: combining 8 copies of the same 80 MB ImageMagick PDF gives a 648 MB file instead of about 81 MB. Pages and rendering are correct. Only the size is affected.

### Repro (origin/main at 5d59060, ImageMagick 7.1.2)

```sh
magick -size 300x200 xc: +noise Random noise.png && magick noise.png in.pdf
pdfcraft-cli combine in.pdf in.pdf in.pdf --out combined.pdf
```

| file | size |
|---|---|
| `in.pdf` | 181,872 |
| `combined.pdf` (3 pages) | 541,628, three copies of the image |

### Cause

ImageMagick writes the image's colour space as a separate indirect object holding a bare name, and points the image at it:

```
10 0 obj
/DeviceRGB
endobj
8 0 obj
<< /Type /XObject /Subtype /Image /ColorSpace 10 0 R ... >>
```

Each source's `/DeviceRGB` object is copied separately. `dedupe.rs::is_resource` only considers streams, resource dictionaries and colour-space arrays, so the bare-name objects are never merged. Because `eq_obj` compares references by (canonical) object number, the copied image dictionaries then differ (`/ColorSpace 18 0 R` vs `19 0 R` vs `20 0 R`), and the images are never merged even though their data is identical.

Confirmed by editing only that entry: the same file with `/ColorSpace /DeviceRGB` written directly (`qpdf --qdf`, replace the reference, `fix-qdf`) combines 3 copies into 181,034 bytes, a single image. Rewriting the file so every `/Length` is direct does not help, so the indirect `/Length` ImageMagick also writes is not the cause.

### Possible fix

When hashing and comparing in `dedupe`, resolve a reference whose target is a plain scalar (name, number, boolean, string, null) and compare the value instead of the object number. Alternatively, inline such scalar objects while copying pages. A regression test could be two sources whose identical images both u…

title: Select tool can't drag a signature that sits over a form field
author: LloydNicholson
body:
## What happens
On a fillable form, a Fill & Sign signature placed on top of a form field can't be moved with the **Select** tool:
- hovering over it shows the Move cursor;
- pressing and dragging does nothing; the signature stays where it is.

Signatures that aren't over a field move normally. With a Fill & Sign tool active (for example **Check**), the same signature over a field does move (since #822).

## Steps to reproduce
1. Open a PDF with text form fields.
2. Choose **Fill & Sign › Sign** and place a signature so that it overlaps a text field.
3. With the **Select** tool (PdfCraft switches to it right after placing), drag the signature at normal hand speed.

**Expected:** the signature moves, as it does anywhere else on the page.
**Actual:** nothing moves.

Reproduced on current `main` (0.5.0, after #822) on Linux (Fedora/KDE Plasma, Wayland), with a drawn signature over the text fields of a government application form.

## Cause
In `crates/ui-egui/src/canvas.rs`, with the Select tool, `forms_ui::page_input` gets the press before `comments::page_input`. Over a field it reports the press as consumed (`is_pointer_button_down_on`). egui only reports `drag_started` a few pixels later. At hand speed the pointer is still over the field at that point, so the comments code never sees the drag start. The cursor still shows Move, because the comment hover sets it after the field does.

A fast drag that leaves the field before `drag_started` fires does work, which is why kittest drags in a few big steps don't catch it.

failed to import supplied dmabufs:

title: Tests: `no_tool_escapes_the_root` fails on Windows when the user can't create symbolic links
author: pauliusiv123-rgb
body:
**What happens**

On Windows as a standard user (no administrator rights, Developer Mode off), `cargo test -p pdfcraft-automation --test hostile_args` fails on main (798650e, Windows 11 x64):

```
root confinement: 510 escape attempts over 141 tools, 495 refused, 15 leaks
  doc_save accepted path="link-out/outside.pdf"
  page_insert_file accepted path="link-out/outside.pdf"
  doc_print accepted path="link-out/outside.pdf"
  doc_optimize accepted path="link-out/outside.pdf"
  ...
15 confinement failure(s); the first is: doc_save accepted path="link-out/outside.pdf"
```

CI doesn't hit it because GitHub's Windows runners run as administrator.

**Why**

The test plants `root/link-out` as a link to the folder outside the root, but ignores the error when the link can't be made:

```rust
#[cfg(windows)]
let _ = std::os::windows::fs::symlink_dir(&base, root.join("link-out"));
```

Creating a symbolic link on Windows needs a privilege that standard users only get with Developer Mode, so here it fails with "A required privilege is not held by the client". Without the link, `link-out/outside.pdf` is an ordinary path inside the root:
- the tools that write a file (`doc_save`, `doc_print`, `doc_optimize`, …) correctly accept it;
- the tools that read one (`page_insert_file`, …) then find the file those writers left there.

Nothing outside the root changes: the test's own check for files created, modified or deleted outside the root finds nothing. So confinement is fine; only the test is wrong.

**Suggested fix**

Try `link-out/outside.pdf` only when the link was actually made, as `staging_never_writes_through_a_symbolic_link_planted_at_its_name` in `crates/automation/src/lib.rs` already does for its own link:

```rust
let linked = std::os::windows::fs::symlink_dir(&base, root.join("link-out"))
    .map_err(|e| eprintln!("symbolic link escapes not checked: {e}"))
    .is_ok();
```

and add `"link-out/outside.pdf"` in `escapes()` only when `linked`.

I can send a PR for this.

title: MCP `doc_create` (from=text) and `page_add_text` replace Korean/CJK characters with `?`
author: pdaw-cowork
body:
**Environment**
- PdfCraft v0.4.0, macOS Apple Silicon (arm64), via MCP server

**Steps to reproduce**
1. MCP `doc_create` with `from=text`, `text="ABC 제안서 시험"` (Latin + Korean).
2. `doc_save` to a file.
3. `text_extract` on the saved document; also `page_render` page 1.

**Expected**
Korean characters are preserved in the text layer and visible in the rendered page (or a clear error/warning if the font cannot encode them).

**Actual**
Latin characters survive; every Korean character becomes `?` in both `text_extract` output and the rendered image (e.g. `ABC ??? ??`). No error or warning is returned.

**Analysis (hypothesis, not verified in source)**
The default font appears to be a PDF standard-14 face without CJK glyphs, so unencodable characters are substituted. `page_add_text` only exposes helvetica / times / courier. Related: #506, #651, #566.

**Suggested fix**
- Fall back to a bundled/system CJK font (embedded subset) when characters fall outside the base font's encoding, and/or
- add a `font` parameter (path or family) to `doc_create` / `page_add_text`, and
- at minimum, return a warning listing unencodable characters instead of silently substituting `?`.

title: Feature request: Sign existing signature fields in permission-restricted PDFs without invalidating prior signatures
author: Eudene21
body:
## Summary
I'd love to use PDFCraft for multi-party signing of official forms, but it currently can't sign PDFs that are permission-encrypted or that already contain a digital signature. Adobe Acrobat Reader handles this workflow, and supporting it would make PDFCraft a real alternative for work documents.

## Current behavior
- Opening a permission-restricted PDF (no open password, AES-256, permissions allow form filling/signing only) in the Sign PDF tool returns an error saying encrypted documents can't be signed.
- If a file with an existing digital signature could be edited, re-saving the whole file would invalidate the earlier signature, since changes aren't appended incrementally.

## Expected behavior
1. **Open permission-restricted PDFs** with an empty user password, and respect their permissions: allow form filling and signing when the "fill forms" permission is granted, and block disallowed actions.
2. **Sign an existing empty signature field** (e.g. a second approver's field) instead of only placing a signature image on the page.
3. **Save as an incremental update**, appending changes to the end of the file so existing digital signatures stay valid.
4. **Optional: certificate-based signing.** Allow signing with a user-supplied digital ID (.pfx/.p12), processed locally in the browser like PDFCraft's other tools.

## Use case
Many workplaces route forms through several approvers. Each person signs their own field, and earlier signatures must remain valid. Today this requires Adobe Acrobat Reader or another desktop app.

## Example file properties
- Encryption: AES-256 (R=6), no user password
- Permissions: fill forms allowed; modify, annotate, assemble, and print not allowed

title: Large documentation PDFs: `text_find` extracts all 9,156 pages before honoring `limit`, retains the full text cache, and makes capped results look complete
author: cyfung1031
body:
## File (publicly accessible from https://techdocs.broadcom.com/us/en/vmware-cis/vcf/vcf-9-0-and-later/9-1.html)

https://techdocs.broadcom.com/content/dam/broadcom/techdocs/us/en/pdf/vmware/vcf/vcf-90/vmware-cloud-foundation-9-1.pdf

## Summary

A current VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x documentation PDF is a useful stress case for PdfCraft's headless text-search path. The file is about 193 MB and reports **9,156 physical pages**. Its running header, `VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x`, is already present on page 1 and then repeats throughout the manual.

On current `main` (`53a5880`), `text_find` does not use `limit` to bound the work. It first asks `page_texts` for **every page in the document**, waits for all missing `PageText` objects to be extracted, stores them in the automation text cache, and only then loops over pages looking for query matches and stops appending matches at the requested limit.

That makes this deliberately easy query:

```json
{"tool":"text_find","args":{"doc":1,"query":"VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x","limit":1}}
```

behave like a whole-document text-extraction job even though the first acceptable result is on page 1.

The same path has three secondary problems that become visible on a document of this size:

- the cached `PageText` data is retained for the document version until the document is closed or the version changes, so a one-result search can populate a whole-document, glyph/geometry-rich cache;
- when the default/explicit match cap is reached, the result only says `"count": N`; there is no `complete`, `truncated`, `has_more`, or continuation field, so `count: 500` can look like the complete result count even when the query has many more matches;
- because all pages are extracted before matching begins, a text-extraction failure on a late page can fail a limited search whose requested result could already have been satisfied thousands of pages earlier.

This is **separate from #307 / #419**. Those changes substantially reduced the co…

title: [Bug]: Releasing Ctrl after zooming keeps scroll behavior locked to zoom (Wayland/COSMIC)
author: rezendepauloh
body:
### Description

When using `Ctrl + Mouse Scroll` to zoom in/out on a PDF document, releasing the `Ctrl` key does not return the scroll wheel to vertical scrolling. The mouse wheel remains stuck in zoom mode, making standard page navigation impossible without restarting or unfocusing/refocusing the application window.

This occurs on both the `.AppImage` and `.deb` releases.

---

**To Reproduce**

1. Open a PDF document in PDFCraft.
2. Scroll up and down using the mouse wheel (normal vertical scrolling functions as expected).
3. Press and hold `Ctrl`, then scroll up/down to zoom in/out.
4. Release the `Ctrl` key.
5. Use the mouse wheel again to scroll vertically.

---

**Expected behavior**

After releasing the `Ctrl` key, mouse wheel input should immediately revert to scrolling the document vertically rather than continuing to adjust the zoom level.

---

**Actual behavior**

The modifier key release event seems to be missed or cached improperly. Even after releasing `Ctrl`, subsequent mouse scroll actions continue to zoom in and zoom out.

---

**Environment**

* **OS:** Pop!_OS 24.04 LTS
* **Desktop Environment:** COSMIC Desktop
* **Display Server:** Wayland
* **Package type:** Tested on both `.deb` and `.AppImage`
* **App Version:** *v0.6.0*

---

**Additional context**

This behavior is common in frameworks (such as Electron, Tauri, or Qt/GTK) when modifier key release events (`keyup`) are not captured properly under Wayland compositors during active scroll events.

title: Feature request (opt-in): shared review and backup on storage you own (local/NAS, Google Drive, OneDrive, S3/R2/WebDAV via rclone), without Acrobat's cloud
author: fernandodilland
body:
## TL;DR
PdfCraft's identity is "no account, no telemetry, no cloud", so this must be strictly opt-in and off by default. Two small features would cover the real collaboration need for PDFs without Adobe's cloud: (1) **shared review**, where comments sync between reviewers over storage the user owns, and (2) **backup/versions** of a document to such storage.

## How Acrobat does it
- **Shared review:** the PDF is posted to a network folder, WebDAV folder, SharePoint or a web service; reviewers are invited by email, add comments, and Acrobat synchronizes comments at regular intervals so everyone sees and replies to each other's comments. Reviewers don't co-edit the document; only comments are shared. There is a deadline, and an email-based review as the alternative.
- Adobe's cloud documents also cover Acrobat, with autosave and sharing through Adobe's storage.

## What PdfCraft has today (README only)
Autosave every minute with a recovery offer, atomic incremental saves (original bytes preserved), threaded comments with replies and status, forms, AES-256 encryption, redaction, an opt-in MCP server, web build.

## Proposal
**Phase 1, backup target:** shared building blocks below. PDF incremental updates are append-only, so upload the base file once and each update as a **small immutable delta object**. Never rewrite a signed document; append only. Encrypted PDFs sync as they are.
**Phase 2, versions:** every incremental update is a natural version; named versions; "restore to this revision" by truncating at an update boundary.
**Phase 3, shared review without a server:** comments live as an **operation log per reviewer** (`reviews/<doc-id>/<reviewer>`), so there are no write conflicts by construction; readers merge by union. Replies reference a parent id; status changes are last-writer-wins; a "closed" marker implements the deadline. A Tracker-style panel shows who has commented. Optionally "bake" the merged comments into the PDF as an incremental update. The review …

title: Enhance camera images: crop and correct perspective from four corners (ocr.camera-perspective)
author: magdale76
body:
Acrobat's *Scan & OCR ▸ Enhance ▸ Camera image* lets the user drag four corner handles around a photographed document; *Enhance page* then crops the page to that quadrilateral and straightens its perspective, so a phone photo of a card or a sheet becomes a flat, rectangular page. In PdfCraft this is `ocr.camera-perspective` (P1, M10, planned), and the All tools catalogue already lists "Enhance scanned file" (`ocr.enhance`) as planned.

I'd like to take this on in two PRs:

1. **Engine + headless tool.** A pure 3×3 homography solve in `geom` (no dependencies), a bilinear perspective warp, and an `Edit` that renders the page at its image's native resolution, warps the chosen quadrilateral to a rectangle and replaces the page content with the result (one undoable step). An automation tool (`page_enhance_camera`: page + four corners in PDF points) with an end-to-end test on a synthetic fixture. Parity → `partial`.
2. **UI.** Four draggable corner handles on the page and an *Enhance page* button, checked through the control channel.

Later, separately: automatic document-edge detection and contrast/background cleanup.

**Relation to #977:** that PR adds deskew/orientation/denoise/binarize as *preprocessing for recognition*, on an internal copy of the raster. This feature changes the page itself and lives in separate files, so the two shouldn't conflict.

Happy to adjust naming or placement if you prefer something else.

body:
## Summary
In Edit PDF → Edit text and images, moving or enlarging an existing image can leave it clipped to its original rectangle. The selection box moves/resizes, but image pixels outside the old region disappear. This was observed in a real PDF exported by Microsoft PowerPoint 2019.

## Steps to reproduce
1. Open a PDF where an image is painted inside a rectangular clipping path (example content below).
2. Choose Edit PDF → Edit text and images.
3. Select the image and drag it beyond its original bounds, or enlarge it.
4. Observe that the image is cut off at the original rectangle instead of remaining fully visible at its new placement.

## Expected

If this case is unsupported, the editor should explain the limitation rather than silently produce a truncated image. A shared clip must not be blindly changed if it also affects other objects.

The image remains visible only through its original fixed clipping region.

title: Enhance camera image: clean up the photo (background, shadows, contrast) with an enhancement level
author: magdale76
body:
Follow-up to #1008 (#1018/#1019/#1027). After *Enhance page* straightens a photographed document, the page still looks like a photo: a grey or yellow cast from room light, a shadow from the phone or a hand, darker edges, noisy text. I'd like to add a clean-up step to the same tool:

- **Background normalisation:** estimate the paper's illumination (a large-scale background estimate) and divide it out, so the sheet becomes white and shadows and edge darkening disappear (`ocr.background-removal`, `ocr.edge-shadow-removal`).
- **Contrast and despeckle:** stretch the text against the cleaned background and drop isolated specks (`ocr.despeckle`).
- **An enhancement level** in the bar after *Enhance page*, from off to strong, with a preview, applied as one undoable step. It always starts again from the straightened photo, so moving the slider never compounds.
- Headless as well: an option on `page_enhance_camera`, with tests on synthetic photos (shadow, colour cast, gradient), plus a check that OCR accuracy on photos improves with the cleanup, using the Italian test pages from #1012's review.

Pure Rust, no new dependencies. It touches only the camera-image code, not the OCR pipeline in #1012/#977, but it should make photos read better there: straighten → clean up → (orientation from #1012) → OCR.

title: [Feature Request] Add OFD (Open Fixed-layout Document) Format Support
author: ufobugs
body:
## Feature Description

I would like to request support for **OFD (Open Fixed-layout Document)**, a standardized fixed-layout document format widely used in China.

OFD is defined by the Chinese national standard **GB/T 33190-2016** and is commonly used in electronic invoices, government documents, and electronic archives.

Adding OFD support would make PdfCraft significantly more useful for Chinese users and organizations.

## Suggested Features

It would be great if PdfCraft could support the following capabilities:

1. **Open and View OFD Files**
   - Open `.ofd` files directly.
   - Render text, images, fonts, and page layouts correctly.
   - Support multi-page documents.

2. **OFD to PDF Conversion**
   - Convert OFD documents into standard PDF files.
   - Preserve the original page layout, fonts, and images as accurately as possible.
   - Support batch conversion if feasible.

3. **PDF to OFD Conversion** (Optional)
   - Export PDF documents to OFD format.

4. **OFD Printing** (Optional)
   - Print OFD documents directly.

## Use Cases

OFD is particularly important in China, where it is used for:

- Electronic invoices (e-Fapiao).
- Government and administrative documents.
- Electronic archives and records management.
- Enterprise document exchange.

Many users regularly receive OFD documents but currently need separate software to open or convert them.

Supporting OFD would allow PdfCraft to provide a more unified document workflow.

## Implementation Considerations

I understand that OFD and PDF are different document formats, and implementing full support may require substantial development effort.

A phased implementation could be considered:

- **Phase 1:** OFD viewing and rendering.
- **Phase 2:** OFD to PDF conversion.
- **Phase 3:** PDF to OFD conversion and additional editing capabilities.

Even basic OFD viewing and OFD-to-PDF conversion would be extremely valuable.

Thank you for developing PdfCraft and considering this feature request.

title: Render: pages with InDesign fades take 5–11 s each (full-page gradient soft masks sampled pixel by pixel)
author: mlkonrad
body:
## Summary

Pages with InDesign fades take several seconds each to render, so a new page often stays blank for a few seconds while you read. A user reported this on both the portable and the ARM64 builds:

> large pdfs take a while to load page-by-page, often having to wait a couple of seconds for a new page to load, would be great if it can be made faster somehow

Firefox (pdf.js) and MuPDF show the same pages almost at once.

## File

*Mobily Annual Report 2025 - English.pdf*, a public annual report (Adobe InDesign 21.2, 144 pages, 16,239,594 bytes):
https://ir.mobily.link/2025/pdfs/Mobily%20Annual%20Report%202025%20-%20English.pdf

SHA-256 `6368c06e2379afdb844861d843bd7b136508b393a1babb210dfdb8640b7e22b6`

## Steps to reproduce

```sh
pdfcraft-cli render "Mobily Annual Report 2025 - English.pdf" --page 4 --dpi 144 --out p4.png
```

Or open the file in the app and go to pages 3, 4 or 80.

## Measurements

`main` (bbbe600), 144 dpi, Linux x86-64 (20 threads). Times include process start:

| Page | PdfCraft | poppler (`pdftoppm`) | MuPDF (`mutool draw`) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 0.67 s | 1.75 s | – |
| 3 | 5.0 s | 2.6 s | – |
| 4 | 10.8 s | 4.7 s | 0.37 s |
| 80 | 9.7 s | 4.1 s | 0.26 s |
| 120 | 1.5 s | 0.67 s | 0.17 s |

Render time grows with pixel count (page 4: 1.0 s at 36 dpi, 2.8 s at 72 dpi, 15.8 s at 144 dpi, 44 s at 288 dpi), so the cost is per pixel.

## Cause

InDesign writes fades and feathers as **luminosity soft masks** (`/SMask << /S /Luminosity /G … >>` in an ExtGState). Each mask's group is a single extended axial shading painted with `sh` over an "infinite" `/BBox [-32768 -32768 32767 32767]`, so it covers the whole page. Page 4 has 40 of them, each a separate mask (no cache hits).

Removing parts of page 4 one at a time (144 dpi):

| Variant | Time |
|---|---|
| unchanged | 15.8 s |
| ExtGState soft masks removed | 0.76 s |
| image soft masks removed | 13.0 s |
| transparency groups removed | 15.7 s |

The vendored hayro 0.7 draws every shading t…

title: Simplified Chinese interface has no usable CJK face: zh-hans UI text renders in wrong/mismatched fonts
author: xuds72
body:
## Environment

- PdfCraft 0.6.0 (macOS dmg build, commit 53a5880386789fc3531e54f6e6ffdef9a8e41f1a)
- macOS (Apple Silicon / Intel both affected — font bundling is build-level, not GPU-level)
- System locale: zh-CN (system language: 简体中文)

## What happens

The `zh-hans` translation catalog ships and the app correctly picks Simplified Chinese for a
zh-CN system locale, so the interface *is* translated — but no embedded face can draw Han
scripts with Simplified coverage. Menu and UI text falls back through the font stack and ends
up degraded: wrong glyph variants and replacement glyphs (tofu) for Simplified-only
characters (e.g. 欢, U+6B6D-range simplifications absent from Japanese faces).

Startup log shows the last-resort fallback resolving to a face with no Han coverage at all:

```
INFO [pdfcraft_ui_egui::system_fonts] interface font fallback: /System/Library/Fonts/SFArabic.ttf
```

## Steps to reproduce

1. Set macOS system language to 简体中文 (or set the `language` preference to `zh-hans`).
2. Launch PdfCraft 0.6.0.
3. Observe the menu bar / home screen text: Chinese labels render with mismatched glyphs
   (Japanese-style variants from the embedded Japanese faces) and tofu for characters those
   faces don't cover.

## Evidence

- The macOS binary embeds these CJK craft-fonts faces only (checked `strings` on
  `PdfCraft.app/Contents/MacOS/PdfCraft` 0.6.0): **BIZ UDPGothic, BIZ UDMincho,
  Shippori Mincho** — all `Jpan`. No `Hans` face is embedded. The dmg's Resources folder even
  carries `OFL-noto-sans-cjk-sc.txt`, but the face itself is not in the binary.
- `crates/fonts/build.rs` skips any family in `BARRED_FAMILIES` (`"Source Han"`, `"Noto Sans
  CJK"`, …), and craft-fonts' Hans coverage is exactly Noto Sans CJK — so in every official
  build `ui_chinese_fonts()` returns an empty list.
- `crates/ui-egui/src/craft.rs` documents this outcome for the without-craft-fonts case
  ("Chinese text then shows the font system's replacement glyph"); with craft-fonts present…

### Is your feature request related to a problem?

- Pinch should zoom only the PDF view, not the rest of the app UI.


### Describe alternatives you've considered

- Keyboard shortcuts (Ctrl +/-): works, but is less discoverable and slower.
- Zoom dropdown/slider in the toolbar: already exists, but isn't gesture-friendly.

Most modern apps (browsers, Adobe Reader, macOS Preview) support touchpad pinch-to-zoom, so its absence feels like a gap in an otherwise smooth touchpad experience. Related existing issues about touchpad scrolling behavior: #759, #289.

- OS: Linux
- Display server: X11 / Wayland

title: Fill & Sign: scan a photographed handwritten signature (paper, shadows and table removed, adjustable)
author: Bjorneseth
body:
Many people want their real handwritten signature on documents. The usual way to get it is to sign a sheet of paper and photograph it with a phone. Today that photo can go through **Add signature ▸ Image**, but the result needs work:

- #637 removes near-white pixels with a fixed cutoff. Its own notes list the limits: "shadows and grey paper can leave a haze. There is no strength slider, checkerboard preview or auto-crop yet."
- A phone photo is rarely white. It has uneven room light, the shadow of the phone or hand, sometimes the table at the edge, and it is much larger than the signature. So the user has to crop and clean it in another program first.
- #220 asks for this: upload an image of a signature and have the background stripped, leaving only the signature, saved for quick reuse. The audit comment keeps that requirement open.

### Proposal

Add a **Scan** tab next to Type / Draw / Image:

1. **Choose photo…** or drop it on the dialog (PNG/JPEG straight from a phone, up to 40 MiB; EXIF orientation applied).
2. **Find the signature.**
   - The signature is framed automatically, all words of it.
   - The sheet edge, the table and dust are ignored.
   - A signature photographed sideways is turned upright.
3. **Adjust.**
   - Move, resize or redraw the frame on the photo.
   - Turn the photo in quarter turns.
   - An **Ink sensitivity** slider (0–100) sets how faint the ink may be (pencil, light ballpoint).
4. **Preview.** It shows the exact result: the ink in its own colour on transparency, trimmed.
5. **Apply.** The result is saved as an ordinary image signature (`SavedSig::Image`). It is remembered between launches and reused, changed or removed like any other signature. The photo and its path are never stored.

How the paper is removed (pure Rust in `pdfcraft-engine`, no new dependencies):

- A grayscale morphological closing (van Herk/Gil-Werman, O(1) per pixel) estimates the paper. It follows lighting gradients and shadow edges.

title: Security review at bbbe600: unpinned downloads in release signing/packaging, plus hardening items
author: christian93kg
body:
I reviewed the source at `bbbe600` (static review plus local builds/tests; nothing was run against any deployed instance). These are the findings, most significant first. Each one has a location and a suggested fix. Items already covered by #987, #1073 or #1099 are left out or cross-referenced.

**One additional finding should be reported privately.** Private vulnerability reporting is disabled on this repo and there's no `SECURITY.md`. Could you enable it (Settings → Code security → Private vulnerability reporting) or share a contact address? I'll send the details there.

---

### 1. `sign.ps1` loads an unpinned NuGet package into `signtool` while signing credentials are in the environment

`packaging/windows/sign.ps1:77`

```powershell
Invoke-WebRequest -Uri 'https://www.nuget.org/api/v2/package/Microsoft.Trusted.Signing.Client' -OutFile $pkg
```

There's no version in the URL, so each release signs with whatever is latest. `Azure.CodeSigning.Dlib.dll` from that package is then loaded into `signtool` while `AZURE_CLIENT_ID`, `AZURE_TENANT_ID`, and `AZURE_CLIENT_SECRET` are set. TLS rules out a network attacker. The exposure is a compromised or bad upstream publish running next to the signing credentials.

**Fix:** pin the version (`.../Microsoft.Trusted.Signing.Client/<version>`) and check a SHA-256 of the `.nupkg` before `Expand-Archive`, the same way `xtask/src/assets.rs` already does for the OCR models. (#1073 doesn't touch this script.)

### 2. AppImage packaging runs `appimagetool` from the mutable `continuous` tag without a hash check

`packaging/linux/package.sh:134`

```bash
curl -fsSL -o "$TOOL" "https://github.com/AppImage/appimagetool/releases/download/continuous/appimagetool-$ARCH.AppImage"
chmod +x "$TOOL"
```

The binary that builds the official AppImage changes whenever upstream pushes to `continuous`. The shared release workflow in #1073 still calls this script.

**Fix:** pin a tagged release and verify its SHA-256 before `chmod +x`.

author: jmacek
body:
Two macOS quit bugs, both reproduced in PdfCraft 0.6.0 on a MacBookPro17,1 (Touch Bar), macOS 26.5.2.

**1. Red close button crashes** (exit 133, SIGTRAP):
```
-[_NSTouchBarFinderObservation invalidate]
___NSTouchBarFinderSetNeedsUpdateOnMain_block_invoke_2
NSDisplayCycleFlush
```
This is the crash tracked in storytold/craft-libs#3 (WordCraft, PhotoCraft, LightCraft, DeckCraft and the Launcher too). eframe drops the window inside AppKit's run loop, and AppKit's Touch Bar code then throws.

**2. Cmd+Q (or PdfCraft › Quit) with unsaved changes quits without asking.** Red close and Dock › Quit ask first. winit's default menu sends Quit straight to `terminate:`, which skips `guard_quit`. Tracked in storytold/craft-libs#20.

**Fix:** adopt `craft-quit` from craft-libs, which PdfCraft already uses for `craft-ui`:
- `craft_quit::on_close_request(ctx)` after `guard_quit` in `logic`, from storytold/craft-libs#5;
- `craft_quit::install_app_menu(&cc.egui_ctx, "PdfCraft")` in the app creator, from storytold/craft-libs#21.

Tested locally with both (a path dependency on #21's branch): red close and Cmd+Q show the unsaved-changes prompt, Cancel keeps the window, Don't Save and a clean Cmd+Q exit 0, and the app menu (Hide ⌘H and the rest) works. A PdfCraft PR can follow once #5 and #21 are merged.

title: Callout: allow repositioning the arrow point, knee and text box independently
author: licjon
body:
### Problem

Once a callout annotation is placed, its arrow point and knee (bend) cannot be repositioned — the only option is to move the entire annotation as a unit. There are also no resize handles on the callout's text box. This makes it difficult to fine-tune where a callout points after placing it.

In Acrobat, the callout's arrow point, knee and text box are all independently draggable, and the text box can be resized while the leader line stays connected.

### Proposed behaviour

1. **Arrow point and knee handles** — when a callout is selected, show draggable handles on the arrow point and the knee. Dragging either repositions it while the text box stays put; the attach point recomputes automatically.
2. **Independent text box move** — dragging the text box body moves only the box. The arrow point and knee stay fixed; the attach point adjusts to the nearest edge.
3. **Text box resize** — the eight standard resize handles appear on the text box boundary (not the outer `/Rect` that includes the leader line). Dragging them resizes the text box; the leader line stays connected.
4. **Live preview** — a temporary leader line follows the drag so the user can see where the arrow will land before releasing.

### Implementation

I have a working implementation across five files (~260 lines) that I can submit as a PR:

- **`crates/annot/src/lib.rs`** — `set_callout_line()` moves the point/knee and recomputes `/CL`, `/Rect`, `/RD` and the appearance. `move_callout_box()` moves only the text box via `apply_text_box()`, keeping the leader line fixed. A `text_box_rect()` helper extracts the text box from `/Rect` + `/RD`.
- **`crates/render/src/inspect.rs`** — exposes `callout_line` (`/CL`) and `rd` (`/RD`) on the `Annotation` struct so the UI knows where the handles go.
- **`crates/engine/src/lib.rs`** — `Edit::MoveCalloutLine` and `Edit::MoveCalloutBox` variants, wired into scope, permissions, undo descriptions and apply.
- **`crates/ui-egui/src/comments.rs`** — `Gesture::…

Fails on CI runners where the workflow checks out `storytold/craft-fonts` and sets
`CRAFT_FONTS_DIR` / `CRAFT_FONTS_REQUIRED=1` (ubuntu-latest, FreeBSD 15). Passes
repeatedly on a local build **without** `CRAFT_FONTS_DIR` set, and the full
`pdfcraft-edit` suite (78 tests) is green there.

Observed at upstream `main` `f036d38` (and on a fork merge of the same commit);
Rust 1.99.0 in both environments.

## Hypothesis

The test mocks the glyph-outline provider, but the hashed bytes include the
serialized fonts dict and the document snapshot. With the real Arab face
available at build time, something in that output (font dictionary bytes and/or
text metrics via `arabic_layout` vs. the no-font fallback width) differs from
the configuration the golden (`SMALL_ITEM_FINGERPRINT`) was recorded in. So the
golden is only valid for one of the two build configurations, and CI exercises
the other.

## Possible fixes

- Make the test hermetic with respect to ambient font availability (e.g. force
  the fallback path, or pin the font-data inputs), or
- record a second golden for the with-`craft-fonts` configuration and select on
  `pdfcraft_fonts::CRAFT_FONTS`.

title: Proposal: Lightweight issue-claiming convention to avoid duplicate work
author: Hathor875
body:
## Summary

This proposal introduces a lightweight, social convention for claiming issues before starting work, to prevent the duplicate-effort collisions we've seen recently. No tooling is required to start; a simple bot/label workflow can be added later if the community finds it useful.

---

## The problem

We've had at least two concrete collisions recently:

1. **Silent fix collision** – A contributor investigated an issue and prepared an implementation, only to discover it had already been fixed in an earlier PR that didn't reference the issue.

2. **Parallel work on #1137 (PPTX export)** – Two contributors independently started implementing the same large feature (#1137), unaware of each other. One had already committed significant work (writer, slide sizing, text boxes) when the other commented "I'll take this one."

With dozens of contributors and 100+ open PRs, these collisions waste contributor time and slow down delivery.

---

## Proposed convention (social, zero-tool start)

| Step | What to do |
|------|------------|
| **1. Claim before coding** | Leave a comment on the issue: `👷 Claiming this — will start by <date>` or open a **Draft PR** (which counts as a claim and links code immediately). |
| **2. Mark it visibly** | Add the `in-progress` label (to be created) and/or assign yourself. |
| **3. Heartbeat** | Post a brief update in the issue or Draft PR **about once a week** (e.g., "still working, hit a snag with X" or "PR coming tomorrow"). |
| **4. Friendly check-in** | If an issue has the `in-progress` label but **about a week passes without an update**, any contributor may leave a friendly check-in comment: `👋 Hey — still active on this? Happy to help or take over if you're blocked.` This is a nudge, not a takeover — contributors are volunteers and may be quiet over weekends or busy periods. |
| **5. Release** | When the PR is merged or you decide to stop, remove the `in-progress` label and unassign yourself. If you step away without finishing, a…

title: Protect accepts passwords that encryption makes empty or identical
author: jay-tau
body:
Protect accepts passwords that encryption makes empty or identical, so the saved file opens without a password, or its open password lifts the restrictions.

## Why
Protect checks the passwords as typed. The encryption keys on a prepared form of each password:
- **AES-256 (the default).** ISO 32000-2 §7.6.4.3.3 has the password processed with SASLprep (RFC 4013), then truncated to 127 bytes of UTF-8. `pdfcraft-crypt` does this in `sasl_password`; if SASLprep refuses a password, it uses the password as given. SASLprep removes U+00AD SOFT HYPHEN, one of the characters RFC 3454 table B.1 maps to nothing. It also applies NFKC, which turns U+FF21 FULLWIDTH LATIN CAPITAL LETTER A into `A`, and U+FB01 LATIN SMALL LIGATURE FI into `fi`. Preparation succeeds for all of these examples.
- **RC4 and AES-128.** The key sees exactly 32 bytes (`legacy_password`, `pad`). Longer passwords are cut there, and shorter ones are filled out with a fixed padding string that starts with `(`.

`Protection::validate` (`crates/engine/src/lib.rs`) checks that each password is non-empty as typed, and that the two differ as typed. Nothing compares the prepared forms.

## What happens on main
These results come from applying `Edit::Protect` in a `Session`, saving, and reopening the saved bytes with `pdfcraft_cos::Document::open_with_password`:

| Algorithm | Open password | Permissions password | Protect | The saved file |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| AES-256 | none | `"\u{AD}"` | accepted | opens with no password, with owner rights |
| AES-256 | `"0"` | `"\u{AD}"` | accepted | opens with no password, with owner rights |
| AES-256 | `"A"` | `"\u{FF21}"` | accepted | the open password gives owner rights |
| AES-256 | `"fi"` | `"\u{FB01}"` | accepted | the open password gives owner rights |
| RC4-128, AES-128 | `"a"` × 32 + `"1"` | `"a"` × 32 + `"2"` | accepted | the open password gives owner rights |
| RC4-128, AES-128 | `"a"` × 31 | `"a"` × 31 + `"("` | accepted | the open password gives owner rights |…

title: Proposal: property-based tests with Hegel for pdfcraft-cos and the editing engine (a pilot found #1185)
author: jay-tau
body:
[Hegel](https://hegel.dev/)'s Rust library, [`hegeltest`](https://docs.rs/hegeltest), is an MIT-licensed property-based testing library based on Hypothesis. You write a property once, it generates inputs, and on failure it shrinks to a small counterexample. It needs no Python: the engine is a Rust library. It is in beta, and its authors say breaking changes are possible.

## Why
`docs/target-app-parity.md` says: "Shipped features rest on thin evidence: 141 of 423 cite exactly one test, and only a handful cite an external oracle (`pdftotext`, `pdfsig`, OpenSSL, `qpdf --check`, a corpus)." A property checks one rule against thousands of generated inputs, which suits `cos`, the layer every file goes through.

## The pilot
I wrote five properties for `pdfcraft-cos` in about 370 lines: https://github.com/jay-tau/pdfcraft/blob/bac29141ec3e346aef97ee940f6526409a913d23/crates/cos/tests/hegel.rs

1. **Object round trip.** Generated non-stream objects survive `serialize` → `Lexer::object`, under a comparison that allows the writer's documented normalisation: integral reals may be written as integers, non-finite reals become zero, and the writer picks literal or hex string syntax. Serialising what was read gives the same bytes.
2. **Full save.** A full save, with or without object streams (drawn per case), reopens without repair and keeps the values reachable from the root. The comparison follows references, so renumbering doesn't matter, and it ignores stream `/Length`.
3. **Editing state machine.** A state machine adds, replaces and frees objects, saves incrementally and reopens, and takes and restores `Document` snapshots. It is checked against a plain map of what each object should be (freed objects must read as null): at the start, at the end, and at sampled steps in between.
4. **Passwords.** This one calls `cos` directly and makes three attempts on a protected file. Without a password it must be `NeedsPassword`; the open password must give user rights, and the permissio…

body:
On macOS every Chrome/Edge launch makes a code-sign clone of the app under /private/var/folders/<user>/X/com.google.Chrome…code_sign_clone; a browser that is killed instead of exiting cleanly never removes it (21 Chrome clones found since 7 Oct; hdb-books had 536 Edge clones). title: PdfCraft PDF Color/Image Semantics Audit
author: cyfung1031
body:
# PdfCraft PDF Color/Image Semantics Audit

**Repository:** `storytold/pdfcraft`  
**Audited revision:** `8ee3673bd434c42daf162b04c725948af75ed130`  
**Scope:** `/DeviceRGB`, `/DeviceGray`, `/DeviceCMYK`, `/ICCBased`, `/Indexed`, `/Decode`, `/DecodeParms`, DCT/JPEG color transforms, CalGray/CalRGB/Lab, Separation/DeviceN, masks, image creation/import, rendering, extraction, optimization/recompression, redaction, resource deduplication, ordinary editing, incremental save, and full save.

## Executive conclusion

**No: the latest `main` does not handle all of these semantics correctly across every subsystem.**

The result is substantially better than a superficial source search suggests, because the actual page renderer uses the vendored Hayro color engine. Rendering has genuine implementations of ICC profiles, Indexed lookup spaces, arbitrary per-component `/Decode` arrays, CalGray/CalRGB/Lab, Separation, DeviceN, soft masks, color-key masks, matte removal, and several image codecs. In that core renderer, `/DeviceRGB`, ordinary `/ICCBased`, `/Indexed`, and general `/Decode` are mostly implemented correctly.   

Ordinary editing and saving are also strong: PdfCraft does not reconstruct image dictionaries from a lossy whitelist. Its COS object layer retains arbitrary dictionaries, arrays, references, and raw stream data; incremental saving writes changed overlay objects, while full saving traverses and renumbers the reachable object graph. Consequently an untouched `/ICCBased` reference, `/Indexed` lookup, `/Decode`, `/DecodeParms`, masks, etc. survive normal editing and saving. 

The weak point is that **pixel-consuming subsystems have independently reimplemented subsets of the renderer's semantics**. Image extraction/export is notably incomplete, optimization has at least one DCT semantic hazard, redaction intentionally handles only a subset of codecs, and the renderer itself has several meaningful color-management gaps.

title: Lab colours ignore the colour space's /WhitePoint (always read as D50)
author: rp6186030
body:
## What's wrong
A `/Lab` colour space whose `/WhitePoint` isn't D50 is drawn in the wrong colours. The renderer reads every Lab value as if the white point were D50, then adapts it to sRGB. ISO 32000-2 §8.6.5.4 defines L\*a\*b\* relative to the space's own `/WhitePoint`.

With `/WhitePoint [0.9505 1 1.089]` (D65), some colours come out visibly off. The blue below is 45 levels too red:

| Lab (D65) | Expected sRGB (CIE formula) | Poppler 24.02 | PdfCraft | Lab read as D50, Bradford-adapted to D65 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 40 20 −60 | 19 90 194 | 19 90 194 | **64 86 194** | 67 86 194 |
| 70 −50 30 | 77 193 114 | 77 193 114 | **63 194 113** | 66 194 113 |
| 60 0 −40 | 87 148 215 | 87 148 215 | **105 147 215** | 105 147 215 |
| 50 60 40 | 217 61 55 | 217 61 55 | 214 60 56 | 214 60 55 |
| 30 40 20 | 130 37 42 | 130 37 42 | 128 37 43 | 128 37 42 |

PdfCraft's values match the last column to within 3 levels, so the `/WhitePoint` is being dropped. Neutral greys (a = b = 0) come out right, which hides the bug on most pages. D50 white points (the usual choice in print workflows) are unaffected.

## Where it likely is
`vendor/hayro-interpret/src/color.rs`, `Lab::new`: it loads the bundled `assets/LAB.icc` and sets `profile.white_point` from the dictionary. A Lab ICC profile's connection space is D50 by definition, though, so the conversion appears to ignore that field. One fix: convert L\*a\*b\* to XYZ with the dictionary's `/WhitePoint`, adapt that XYZ to D50 (Bradford), and only then hand it to the colour transform. Alternatively, convert straight to sRGB as Poppler does.

## How to reproduce
A 200 × 200 pt page with this resource and content:

```
/Resources << /ColorSpace << /L [/Lab << /WhitePoint [0.9505 1 1.089] /Range [-100 100 -100 100] >>] >> >>

/L cs
40 20 -60 sc 20 20 160 160 re f
```

`pdfcraft-cli render page.pdf --page 1 --dpi 72 --out x.png` draws the square as 64 86 194; `pdftoppm` draws 19 90 194.

The `lab` page of `cargo xtask render-oracle` (#1163) has ni…

body:
**Title:** Korean (Hangul) text shows as tofu boxes in UI text fields (search, bookmarks)

## Summary
Hangul characters are not displayed in PrintCraft's own UI text fields, such as the
find bar and the bookmark/outline editor. Hangul inside PDF pages renders correctly
(embedded fonts), so this only affects the application UI.

## Steps to reproduce
1. Open any PDF.
2. Open the find bar (or edit a bookmark title).
3. Paste or type Korean text, e.g. `한글 검색`.

## Expected behavior
The Korean text is displayed and can be searched/edited.

## Actual behavior
Each Hangul character is shown as a tofu box (□). Pasting from the clipboard shows
the same boxes, so the text appears to be received but cannot be drawn.

## Environment
- PrintCraft version / commit: [version or commit hash]
- OS: [Windows 11 / macOS / Linux distro]
- Install method: [release binary / built from source]
- System language / IME: Korean

## Possible cause (not verified)
The UI is built on egui, whose default fonts contain no Hangul glyphs. The only
bundled CJK fonts appear to be the Japanese ones from `craft-fonts`, so there is
no Korean fallback font registered in the UI font definitions.

## Suggested direction
Register a Hangul-capable fallback font (e.g. Noto Sans KR, SIL OFL) in
`egui::FontDefinitions` for both Proportional and Monospace families, or load a
system CJK font at runtime when available. Related: ROADMAP lists CJK editing and
localization as incomplete, so this may fit under that work.

## Additional notes
Korean in PDF page content is unaffected. A related question is whether Hangul text
entered into annotations/form fields can get correct appearance streams, since
those would need Hangul glyphs as well.

body:
### Description
PdfCraft currently defaults to `ThemePreference::Light` on fresh installs and initial startup rather than following the host desktop's appearance settings (`ThemePreference::System`). As a result, when launched on an operating system configured for dark mode (e.g., Linux GNOME/KDE, macOS, Windows), the interface renders in light mode unless manually toggled.

Furthermore, viewing documents does not automatically adjust or provide an option to render document pages in dark mode (screen-only dark page appearance / night reading mode) following the system or application theme preference.

### Current Behavior
- `ThemePreference::default()` and `PdfCraftApp::default().theme_preference` default to `ThemePreference::Light`.
- Fresh installs and first launches on dark desktop environments start in Light mode, ignoring the system setting.
- Document pages render with standard white paper background regardless of the system/app theme.

### Desired Behavior
1. Default the application UI theme preference to `ThemePreference::System` ("Use system setting") so that the window chrome and interface automatically render in dark mode when the OS prefers dark appearance.
2. Support dark mode document page rendering (screen-only dark page appearance) that respects the system/application dark theme, darkening paper and adapting vector and text paints while preserving embedded raster images and export output.

title: Support for Classic Acrobat Layout & RTL/BiDi Bookmark Reordering
author: ClJoussour
body:
### Support for Classic Acrobat Layout & RTL/BiDi Bookmark Reordering

I strongly support adding an optional **Classic GUI Layout** (similar to Adobe Acrobat's classic view / "Disable new Acrobat" mode):

1. **Left-Hand Navigation Pane:** Bookmarks and page thumbnails anchored on the **left side** rather than the right rail. For reading long books and manuscripts, having the table of contents on the left is standard and far more ergonomic.
2. **Top Menu & Command Toolbar:** A persistent top menu bar (`File`, `Edit`, `View`, `Window`) and an optional horizontal top toolbar containing core navigation tools (Page input `[ 1 / N ]`, Zoom controls, Hand/Select tools) instead of the floating in-page tool pill.
3. **Arabic/RTL Bookmark Ordering in Outline:** In v0.6.0, Arabic font glyphs render nicely thanks to system font fallback and Noto Sans Arabic, but multi-line / outline bookmark titles in `crates/ui-egui/src/panels.rs` (`outline_item`) still need `bidi::visual_auto` / visual reordering so words don't appear in reversed logical order.

Adding a toggle setting (e.g. `View -> Layout -> Classic / Modern`) would make PdfCraft the ultimate Acrobat replacement for millions of users who prefer the traditional workflow.

title: Explain blank legacy Flash/SWF PDF diagrams and offer safe extraction
author: earlvanze
body:
## Request
A user has a Mazda 3 service manual whose wiring diagrams are embedded as Flash/SWF content. The pages appear blank in PdfCraft. They need a way to access those diagrams.

## Current status
`parity/acrobat-features.toml` marks `misc.flash-swf` as N/A, with content preserved but not played. Rich-media poster and platform video/sound playback are planned for M12; neither provides SWF playback. No open issue or PR specifically covers access to legacy SWF diagrams.

## Scope
Investigate a safe fallback for PDFs with embedded SWF: detect the content, explain why the page is blank, and offer extraction of the embedded asset when possible. Do not promise or enable Flash execution.

## Acceptance criteria
- Detect embedded Flash/SWF content and show an actionable explanation instead of an unexplained blank region.
- If feasible, let the user save the embedded asset without executing it.
- Preserve the original PDF content when saving.
- Document the limitation and a practical path to view or convert legacy diagrams externally.

title: Make the highlighter quick-click regression test deterministic
author: cyfung1031
body:
related: #1168, #1171 

## Summary

This is a focused follow-up to item 1 of #1168. The test `quick_clicks_with_the_highlighter_mark_only_the_word` was reported to fail intermittently in the shared `ui_group` test binary. A later attempt to move it into a standalone Cargo integration-test target also failed intermittently, so restoring the process boundary alone did not establish a reliable fix. That process-isolation change was not submitted.

Make the regression test reliable without weakening its assertions. Change product click behavior only if a deterministic user-facing defect is separately reproduced.

## Evidence

- [Issue #1168](https://github.com/storytold/pdfcraft/issues/1168) reports that, at commit `49217aec6c616056d58c3258a60ab30bce0fd701`, the grouped `ui_group` target failed in 2 of 5 Windows 11 x64 runs. The reported failure was `assert!(app.views[0].selected_text().is_none())`; running the test alone passed 3 of 3 runs.
- During follow-up investigation, the same test also failed intermittently after being moved to a standalone integration-test target. The available record does not include a pass/fail denominator for those runs.
- The description of [PR #1165](https://github.com/storytold/pdfcraft/pull/1165) independently records this test failing in 1 of 6 runs on a previous commit.
- The test performs four simulated clicks, then checks for exactly one Highlight with one quad and no remaining text selection (`crates/ui-egui/tests/ui_group/text_select.rs`).

## Investigation lead

Applying a comment edit calls `page_changed`, which removes the cached page text and clears selection (`crates/ui-egui/src/editing.rs`, `crates/ui-egui/src/canvas.rs`). This is a timing boundary worth investigating, but the available evidence does not establish it as the cause.

## Expected result

The test should reliably verify that quick clicks with the Highlighter create one mark on the word and leave no text selected.

title: Fill & Sign: manage and reuse multiple saved signatures
author: earlvanze
body:
Request from kd4tee in ArtCraft #pdfcraft📄 on 2026-10-12.

Current source stores one saved signature and one initials entry, with add/change/remove controls. A placed signature can be selected, moved and resized, but the saved-signature picker cannot hold several signatures or switch between them.

Add a collection of named or distinguishable saved signatures with a clear picker, while preserving existing saved data. Support placing the same saved signature on multiple pages and independently editing each placed annotation. Consider a duplicate action for a placed signature and clarify copy/paste behavior. This is for Fill & Sign appearance signatures, not cryptographic digital signatures.

body:

Existing page clipboard gestures and Create PDF from Clipboard do not cover this workflow. Include platform and format handling for copied file URLs and bitmap clipboard data.
